passages.title: The Pencil Case on the Art Cart
passages.body: After art class, Aoi saw a blue pencil case on the art cart. Two classes used the cart that day, so she did not know its owner. A small rabbit sticker was on the case. Aoi checked the supply record beside the art room door. The record said that Class 1-3 had a blue case with a rabbit mark. She also asked the art teacher before moving it. The teacher looked at the record and agreed. Aoi carried the case to Class 1-3. She used two clues and did not give it to the wrong class.
passages.fullTranslation: 美術の授業の後、アオイは美術用のワゴンの上に青い筆箱を見つけました。その日は二つのクラスがワゴンを使っていたので、持ち主は分かりませんでした。筆箱には小さなウサギのシールが付いていました。アオイは美術室のドアのそばにある備品記録を確認しました。記録には、1年3組がウサギの印の付いた青い筆箱を使っているとありました。アオイは動かす前に美術の先生にも確認しました。先生も記録を見て確かめました。アオイは筆箱を1年3組へ届けました。二つの手がかりを使ったので、間違ったクラスへ渡さずにすみました。

passages.title: A Red Clip on the Homework Box
passages.body: Yuki came to school with homework from the day before. Near the teacher's desk, there were two homework boxes. One box had a red clip, and the other had a white clip. Yuki almost put his paper in the first box he saw. Then he read the instructions on the board. They said, “Red clip: late homework. White clip: today's homework.” Yuki looked at his paper again and chose the red box. Later, the teacher found his work quickly. Yuki was glad that he read the board before putting the paper away.
passages.fullTranslation: ユキは前日の宿題を持って学校へ来ました。先生の机の近くには宿題箱が二つありました。一方には赤いクリップ、もう一方には白いクリップが付いていました。ユキは最初に目に入った箱へ紙を入れそうになりましたが、黒板の説明を読みました。そこには「赤いクリップ：遅れて出す宿題、白いクリップ：今日の宿題」とありました。ユキはもう一度自分の紙を見て、赤い箱を選びました。あとで先生はその宿題をすぐに見つけられました。ユキは、紙を入れる前に黒板を読んでよかったと思いました。

passages.title: The Shoes beside the Stage
passages.body: Before rehearsal, Ken found two pairs of white indoor shoes beside the stage. His pair was missing from the usual shelf. The two pairs looked the same from the front. Ken did not try either pair. He turned them around and checked the numbers written inside. One pair had 1-1, and the other had 1-4. Ken was in Class 1-4. He took the second pair and put the first pair near the Class 1-1 bags. A classmate thanked him later. Checking the class number solved the problem without any guessing.
passages.fullTranslation: リハーサルの前、ケンは舞台のそばに白い上履きが二足あるのを見つけました。いつもの棚には自分の上履きがありませんでした。二足は前から見ると同じに見えました。ケンはどちらも履いてみず、向きを変えて内側に書かれた番号を確認しました。一足には1-1、もう一足には1-4とありました。ケンは1年4組です。そこで二足目を取り、一足目は1年1組のかばんの近くへ置きました。あとでクラスメートがお礼を言いました。クラス番号を確認したので、当てずっぽうにせず問題を解決できました。

passages.title: The Light Left On in Room Two
passages.body: Maya walked past Room Two after school and saw that its light was still on. No students were inside. She first thought someone forgot the light, and she reached for the switch. Then she noticed a small paper on the door. It said that the cleaning team would use Room Two from four thirty. Maya checked the club schedule on the wall too. The room had no club activity that evening, but the cleaning time started in ten minutes. She left the light on and went to find the teacher. The teacher said the cleaners needed a bright room. Later, the cleaners brought in their equipment. A few minutes later, Maya saw two cleaners arrive with boxes. She understood why the room was ready before they came. She first looked only through the window. That was the wrong choice. The note and the schedule showed the full answer.

passages.title: Which Folder Goes to the Office?
passages.body: Sora took one folder from the classroom to the school office for the teacher. On the teacher's table, there were two gray folders. One had a blue tab and one had an orange tab. Sora did not remember it. He checked the delivery list beside the door. It said, “Office: blue tab. Library: orange tab.” Sora took the blue folder. Before leaving, he showed it to another student. That student was also on delivery duty. They checked the list together. The folder reached the office, and the orange one stayed for the library.
passages.fullTranslation: ソラは教室から学校の事務室へ一冊のファイルを届けることになっていました。先生の机には灰色のファイルが二冊あり、一冊には青い見出し、もう一冊にはオレンジ色の見出しが付いていました。先生がどちらと言ったか、ソラは思い出せませんでした。そこでドアのそばの配達一覧を確認しました。そこには「事務室：青、図書室：オレンジ」とありました。ソラは青いファイルを取りました。出る前に、同じ配達係の生徒にも見せ、二人で一覧を確認しました。青いファイルは事務室へ届き、オレンジのものは図書室用に残りました。

passages.title: The Name Card near the Sink
passages.body: Hina found a name card on the floor near the classroom sink. The printed name was wet, and she read only the first letter, M. Three students in the class had names beginning with M. Hina looked at the seating chart, but that did not show the card’s owner. Then she remembered the class photo on the wall. In the photo, one student had the same green star on her name card. Hina checked the star and returned the card to Miki. Miki smiled and said she had dropped it while washing her hands.
passages.fullTranslation: ヒナは教室の流しの近くの床で名札を見つけました。印刷された名前はぬれていて、最初のMしか読めませんでした。クラスにはMで始まる名前の生徒が三人いました。ヒナは座席表を見ましたが、それだけでは誰が名札をなくしたのか分かりませんでした。そこで壁のクラス写真を思い出しました。写真では、一人の生徒の名札に同じ緑の星が付いていました。ヒナは星を確かめて、ミキに名札を返しました。ミキは笑って、手を洗ったときに落としたのだと言いました。

sentences: Hina found a name card
on the floor near the classroom sink.
The printed name was wet,
and she read only the first letter, M.
Three students in the class
had names beginning with M.
Hina looked at the seating chart,
but that did not show the card’s owner.
Then she remembered
the class photo on the wall.
In the photo,
one student had the same green star
on her name card.
Hina checked the star
and returned the card to Miki.
Miki smiled
and said she had dropped it
while washing her hands.

passages.title: The Bus Stop with Two Signs
passages.body: After a school event, Ryo saw a first-year student between two bus signs near the gate. The student wanted the bus to East Station, but both signs had the word East on them. Ryo first looked at the route numbers. One sign showed Route 5, and the other showed Route 8. He did not know the correct number, so he checked the departure sheet attached to the gate. It said that the 4:20 bus to East Station was Route 8. Route 5 went to East Park at 4:25. Ryo showed the student both the place name and the time. They moved to the Route 8 line. Soon a bus arrived with “East Station” on the front. Ryo stayed until the student got on. He learned that one familiar word on a sign was not enough. The route number, full place name, and departure time all helped him give safe directions.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校行事の後、リョウは校門近くの二つのバス案内の間で迷っている一年生を見つけました。その生徒は東駅へ行くバスに乗りたかったのですが、どちらの案内にも「東」という言葉がありました。リョウはまず路線番号を見ました。一方は5番、もう一方は8番でした。正しい番号が分からなかったので、校門に付けられた出発表を確認しました。そこには、4時20分発の東駅行きは8番だとありました。5番は4時25分発で東公園へ行きます。リョウは生徒に行き先の名前と時刻の両方を見せました。二人は8番の列へ移りました。まもなく前面に「東駅」と表示されたバスが来ました。リョウはその生徒が乗るまで一緒にいました。案内の中の知っている一語だけでは十分ではないと分かりました。路線番号、行き先の完全な名前、出発時刻の三つが、安全に案内する助けになりました。

passages.title: A Sticker on the Science Box
passages.body: After science class, Miku found a small box under a desk. It held two magnets and a piece of string. A moon sticker was on the lid. Three groups had used similar boxes, so Miku checked the experiment list on the board. The list showed a sun mark for Group A, a moon mark for Group B, and a star mark for Group C. Miku carried the box to Group B's table. The students there counted the magnets and thanked her. She also told the teacher where she found it. Then the class checked the room again.
passages.fullTranslation: 理科の授業の後、ミクは机の下に小さな箱を見つけました。中には磁石が二つとひもが一本入っていました。ふたには月のシールが付いていました。三つの班が似た箱を使っていたので、ミクは黒板の実験一覧を確認しました。一覧にはA班は太陽、B班は月、C班は星の印とありました。ミクは箱をB班の机へ運びました。班の生徒たちは磁石の数を確かめて、お礼を言いました。ミクは先生にも見つけた場所を伝えたので、ほかに不足している物がないかクラスで確認できました。

passages.title: The Towel on the Fence
passages.body: After sports practice, Taichi saw a white towel on the fence. Two teams had practiced on the field. The towel had no name, so he did not carry it to either team. He checked the sports-day duty chart near the equipment room. The chart said that the relay team used white towels that day, while the ball team used blue ones. Taichi took the towel to the relay team's basket and told the teacher where he found it. A student came back for it a few minutes later. Taichi's small check saved the student from searching around the whole field.
passages.fullTranslation: 運動練習の後、タイチはフェンスに白いタオルが掛かっているのを見つけました。二つのチームが運動場で練習していました。タオルには名前がなかったので、どちらかのチームへすぐ持っていくことはしませんでした。用具室の近くにある運動会の係表を確認すると、その日はリレーチームが白いタオルを使い、ボールのチームは青いタオルを使うとありました。タイチは白いタオルをリレーチームのかごへ持っていき、見つけた場所を先生に伝えました。数分後、一人の生徒が取りに戻ってきました。タイチが少し確認したことで、その生徒は運動場中を探さずにすみました。

passages.title: Why the Classroom Door Was Open
passages.body: Nana walked into the hallway during lunch and noticed that the door of an empty classroom was wide open. It was a cold day, and she thought the room would become too cold. She started to close the door, but a notice beside the handle caught her eye. It said, “Please keep this door open from 12:30 to 1:00.” Nana checked the lesson schedule too. The next class was a science activity that used a safe but strong-smelling liquid. The teacher wanted fresh air in the room before students arrived. Nana left the door open and moved a chair that was blocking part of the doorway. At one o'clock, the science teacher came and thanked her for following the notice. Nana had wanted to help by closing the door, but she learned that the open door was also part of a plan. Reading the notice before acting changed her decision.
passages.fullTranslation: 昼休み、ナナは廊下を歩いていて、誰もいない教室のドアが大きく開いていることに気づきました。寒い日だったので、教室が冷えすぎると思いました。ドアを閉め始めましたが、取っ手の横の掲示が目に入りました。そこには「12時30分から1時まではこのドアを開けておいてください」とありました。ナナは理由が気になり、授業予定も確認しました。次の授業は、強いにおいのする安全な液体を使う理科の活動でした。先生は生徒が来る前に新しい空気を教室へ入れておきたかったのです。ナナはドアを開けたままにし、出入口を少しふさいでいたいすを移動しました。1時になると理科の先生が来て、掲示どおりにしてくれたことを感謝しました。ナナはドアを閉めることが手助けになると思っていましたが、開けておくことも計画の一部だと分かりました。行動する前に掲示を読んだことで判断が変わりました。

passages.title: The Lunch Tray with a Green Mark
passages.body: Koki helped carry lunch trays to four tables. One tray had a green mark on the corner. He almost put it on the nearest table, but he remembered a food note from the teacher. Koki checked the note beside the lunch cart. It said, “Green tray: Table Four. No eggs for one student.” Koki carried the tray to Table Four and told the student about the mark. The other trays had no green mark. By checking the note, Koki gave the special lunch to the right person without calling attention to the student in front of everyone.
passages.fullTranslation: コウキは四つのテーブルへ給食のトレーを運ぶ手伝いをしていました。一枚のトレーの角には緑の印がありました。いちばん近いテーブルへ置きそうになりましたが、先生からの食べ物についてのメモを思い出しました。給食ワゴンの横のメモを見ると、4番テーブルの一人の生徒は卵を食べられないため、緑のトレーは4番テーブル用だとありました。コウキはそのトレーを4番テーブルへ運び、印についてその生徒に伝えました。ほかのトレーには緑の印はありませんでした。メモを確認したので、みんなの前でその生徒を目立たせることなく、特別な給食を正しい人へ渡せました。

passages.title: A Number on the Library Card
passages.body: Rina found a library card between two books after reading time. The name side was under a clear cover, but the clear cover showed number 24. Rina checked the small shelf list near the reading corner. Each student had a numbered place for returned books. Number 24 belonged to Daiki. Rina did not put the card in his bag. She gave it to the librarian and explained what she had checked. The librarian called Daiki, and he confirmed the card was his. Rina used the number as a clue but still asked an adult to finish the return safely.
passages.fullTranslation: 読書の時間の後、リナは二冊の本の間に図書カードを見つけました。名前の面は透明なカバーの下で見えにくくなっていましたが、24という番号はよく見えました。リナは読書コーナー近くの小さな棚の一覧を確認しました。返却した本を置く場所には、生徒ごとの番号が付いていました。24番はダイキの番号でした。リナはカードを勝手に彼のかばんへ入れず、司書に渡して自分が確認したことを説明しました。司書がダイキを呼ぶと、本人が自分のカードだと確認しました。リナは番号を手がかりにしましたが、安全に返す最後の確認は大人に頼みました。

passages.title: The Chair Facing the Window
passages.body: Yuma entered the classroom before afternoon lessons and saw one chair facing the window instead of the front board. He thought someone had moved it as a joke. The chair was in a walking space, so Yuma wanted to put it back at once. Then he noticed a note on the teacher's desk. It said that the art class would draw the old tree outside the west window. Yuma checked the afternoon plan on the board. Art was the first lesson, and the note asked students not to move the marked chair. A small piece of tape under the chair matched the mark on the note. Yuma left it where it was and moved his own bag away from the walking space. During art class, the teacher used that chair to show students a good viewing place. After the lesson, the chair went back to its desk. Yuma learned that something unusual in a room can have a clear purpose. He checked before changing it.
passages.fullTranslation: 午後の授業前、ユウマが教室へ入ると、一脚のいすだけが前の黒板ではなく窓の方を向いていました。誰かがいたずらで動かしたのだと思いました。いすは通る場所にあったので、ユウマはすぐ戻そうとしました。すると先生の机の上のメモに気づきました。そこには、美術の授業で西側の窓の外にある古い木を描くと書かれていました。ユウマは黒板の午後の予定も確認しました。最初の授業は美術で、印の付いたいすを動かさないよう書かれていました。いすの下の小さなテープはメモの印と同じでした。ユウマはいすをそのままにし、自分のかばんを通路から移しました。美術の授業では、先生がそのいすを使って木がよく見える場所を生徒に示しました。授業後、いすは元の机へ戻されました。教室の中で変わって見える物にも、はっきりした目的があることをユウマは学びました。変える前に確認したのです。

passages.title: The Small Bell in the Gym Bag
passages.body: Akari found a small silver bell beside a gym bag after club time. She saw a red bag, so she first thought the bell belonged to the red-team cheer group. Then she saw a number on the bell. Akari checked the equipment list on the gym wall. Number 12 was a dance club bell used in one song. The cheer group did not have bells on its list. Akari took the bell to the dance club leader and explained where she found it. The leader had been looking for it. The bag color was only a nearby clue; the number and list gave the answer.
passages.fullTranslation: 部活動の後、アカリは体育館のかばんのそばに小さな銀色のベルを見つけました。かばんが赤かったので、最初は赤組の応援グループの物だと思いました。するとベルに番号があるのを見つけました。アカリが体育館の壁の用具一覧を確認すると、12番はダンス部が一曲で使うベルでした。応援グループの一覧にはベルがありませんでした。アカリはベルをダンス部のリーダーへ持っていき、見つけた場所を説明しました。リーダーはちょうど探していました。かばんの色は近くにあっただけの手がかりで、番号と一覧が答えを示しました。

passages.title: A Yellow Arrow by the Stairs
passages.body: Kenta saw a yellow arrow on the floor near the stairs. It pointed away from the usual route to the classrooms. He first said, “This arrow is for a game.” Before following it, he read a sign on the wall. The sign said, “Health check today. Follow the yellow arrows to Room 5.” Kenta had a health check after lunch, so he followed the arrow. The route used a quieter hallway and kept students away from another class. He reached Room 5. A teacher was waiting there. The temporary arrow made sense after Kenta read the sign.

passages.title: The Poster Taken Down Before Friday
passages.body: Mei came to the hallway on Thursday and saw that a music-event poster was no longer on the wall. The event was on Friday, so she thought someone had removed the poster too early. She found it carefully placed on a table nearby. Mei was about to put it back. Then she noticed a message from a teacher beside it. The message said that new fire-safety information needed that wall until Friday morning. Mei checked the event calendar too. The music event would start after lunch on Friday, so the club planned to return the poster before students needed the final reminder. She left the poster on the table and spoke to her club leader about it. On Friday morning, the safety notice came down, and the club put the event poster back in the same place. Mei understood that taking the poster down was not a mistake. Two school activities needed the same wall at different times, and the teacher's message explained the order.
passages.fullTranslation: 木曜日、メイが廊下へ行くと、音楽行事のポスターが壁からなくなっていました。行事は金曜日なので、誰かが早く外しすぎたのだと思いました。近くのテーブルに丁寧に置かれているポスターを見つけ、戻そうとしましたが、その横に先生からのメッセージがあることに気づきました。そこには、新しい防火のお知らせを金曜日の朝までその壁に掲示する必要があると書かれていました。メイは行事予定表も確認しました。音楽行事は金曜日の昼食後に始まるので、最後のお知らせが必要になる前にポスターを戻せます。メイはポスターをテーブルに置いたまま、分かったことを部のリーダーへ伝えました。金曜日の朝、防火のお知らせが外され、部員たちは同じ場所へ行事のポスターを戻しました。ポスターを外したのは間違いではなかったのです。二つの学校活動が別々の時間に同じ壁を必要としていて、先生のメッセージが順番を説明していました。

passages.title: The Blue Dot on the Seating Map
passages.body: Before an open-school event, Haruto helped arrange chairs in the hall. One chair had a blue dot on the seating map, but there was no name beside it. Haruto thought it was an extra chair and started to move it. Then he checked the map key in the corner. A blue dot meant “visitor seat.” The chair was for a guest who needed to sit near the door. Haruto returned it to the marked place and moved a different empty chair instead. The guest arrived and saw the seat. The small map key stopped Haruto from changing an important part of the seating plan.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校公開行事の前、ハルトはホールのいすを並べる手伝いをしていました。座席図では一つのいすに青い点が付いていましたが、横に名前はありませんでした。ハルトは予備のいすだと思い、動かし始めました。そこで図の隅にある記号の説明を確認しました。青い点は「来客用の席」という意味でした。そのいすはドアの近くに座る必要がある来客のためのものでした。ハルトは印の場所へ戻し、代わりに別の空いたいすを動かしました。来客が到着したとき、その席はすぐ見つかりました。小さな記号の説明を確認したことで、大切な座席計画を変えずにすみました。

Haruto helped arrange chairs
in the hall.
One chair had a blue dot
on the seating map,
but there was no name beside it.
Haruto thought
it was an extra chair
and started to move it.
Then he checked the map key
in the corner.
A blue dot meant
“visitor seat.”
The chair was for a guest
who needed to sit near the door.
Haruto returned it
to the marked place
and moved a different empty chair instead.
The guest arrived
and saw the seat.
The small map key stopped Haruto
from changing an important part
of the seating plan.

passages.title: The Water Bottle Return Survey
passages.body: The environmental committee placed two water-bottle return boxes in the school. After one week, the box near the gym was almost full, but the box beside the library had only a few bottles. Some students said the library box was unnecessary. Before removing it, the committee watched students in the area. They found that many students walked past the library box without noticing it because a tall plant covered the sign. The students moved the sign above the plant and added an arrow. During the next week, the number of returned bottles there doubled. The problem was not the location of the box but the way students saw it. They also asked five students to point to the box before and after the change. Four more students noticed it after the sign was moved.
passages.fullTranslation: 環境委員会は校内に二つのペットボトル返却箱を置きました。一週間後、体育館近くの箱はほぼいっぱいでしたが、図書室横の箱には数本しか入っていませんでした。図書室の箱は必要ないという生徒もいました。しかし撤去する前に、委員会は生徒たちがその場所をどう使うか観察しました。すると、背の高い植物が表示を隠していたため、多くの生徒が箱に気づかず通り過ぎていると分かりました。生徒たちは表示を植物より高い位置へ移し、矢印も付けました。次の一週間で、その場所の返却本数は二倍になりました。問題は箱の場所ではなく、生徒からどう見えるかでした。 さらに変更の前後で5人の生徒に箱の場所を指してもらうと、表示を移した後は気づける生徒が4人増えました。

questions.prompt: What did the committee discover about the poorly used library return box?
questions.answer: The box itself was not in the wrong place; students often failed to notice it because the sign was hidden.
questions.evidence: The problem was not the location of the box but the way students saw it.
questions.evidenceJp: 問題は箱の場所ではなく、生徒からどう見えるかでした。
questions.reason: Moving the sign rather than the box increased returns, showing visibility was the main issue.

questions.prompt: What was hiding the sign near the library box?
questions.answer: A tall plant.
questions.evidence: They found that many students walked past the library box without noticing it because a tall plant covered the sign.
questions.evidenceJp: すると、背の高い植物が表示を隠していたため、多くの生徒が箱に気づかず通り過ぎていると分かりました。
questions.reason: The plant blocked the visual cue that told students about the return box.

questions.prompt: Why did the committee observe students before removing the library box?
questions.answer: They wanted to understand why students were not using it before deciding that the box was unnecessary.
questions.evidence: Before removing it, the committee watched students in the area.
questions.evidenceJp: しかし撤去する前に、委員会は生徒たちがその場所をどう使うか観察しました。
questions.reason: Observation let them test whether low use came from the box's location or another cause.

questions.prompt: What change did the students make to the sign?
questions.answer: They moved it above the plant and added an arrow.
questions.evidence: The students moved the sign above the plant and added an arrow.
questions.evidenceJp: 生徒たちは表示を植物より高い位置へ移し、矢印も付けました。
questions.reason: The change made the return box easier to notice without relocating it.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: After the sign became easier to see, the number of returned bottles at the library box ____.
questions.answer: doubled
questions.evidence: During the next week, the number of returned bottles there doubled.
questions.evidenceJp: 次の一週間で、その場所の返却本数は二倍になりました。
questions.reason: The increase provided evidence that visibility affected use.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the committee keep the box in the same location during the change?
questionSetB.answer: So they could see whether improving visibility alone would change student behavior.
questionSetB.evidence: The problem was not the location of the box but the way students saw it.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 問題は箱の場所ではなく、生徒からどう見えるかでした。
questionSetB.reason: Changing only the sign made it easier to connect the later increase to visibility rather than a new box location.

questionSetB.prompt: How many students did the committee ask to point to the box before and after the change?
questionSetB.answer: Five students.
questionSetB.evidence: They also asked five students to point to the box before and after the change.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: さらに変更の前後で5人の生徒に箱の場所を指してもらうと、表示を移した後は気づける生徒が4人増えました。
questionSetB.reason: The five-student check gave an additional measure of whether the box became easier to notice.

questionSetB.prompt: What additional result supported the idea that the new sign was easier to notice?
questionSetB.answer: Four more students could identify the box after the sign was moved.
questionSetB.evidence: Four more students noticed it after the sign was moved.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: さらに変更の前後で5人の生徒に箱の場所を指してもらうと、表示を移した後は気づける生徒が4人増えました。
questionSetB.reason: The pointing test supported the bottle-return result with direct evidence about visibility.

questionSetB.prompt: What does 'unnecessary' mean when some students described the library box that way?
questionSetB.answer: Not needed or not useful enough to keep.
questionSetB.evidence: Some students said the library box was unnecessary.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 図書室の箱は必要ないという生徒もいました。
questionSetB.reason: They were suggesting removal because the box appeared to receive very few bottles.

questionSetB.prompt: What general lesson does the survey demonstrate?
questionSetB.answer: Before removing something that seems unused, investigate whether people can notice and understand how to use it.
questionSetB.evidence: Before removing it, the committee watched students in the area.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: しかし撤去する前に、委員会は生徒たちがその場所をどう使うか観察しました。
questionSetB.reason: The investigation revealed a fixable visibility problem that would have been missed by judging only the first week's totals.

passages.title: A Reminder Sent at the Wrong Time
passages.body: The tennis club sent practice reminders every morning at seven. Still, several members often forgot to bring special shoes for after-school practice. The club leader thought the messages were too short, but one student suggested checking when members actually read them. For five days, members recorded the time they opened the reminder. Most did not look at their phones before school. They read the message around lunch or after classes. At that time, they were at school and the shoes were at home. The club changed the reminder to eight o'clock the night before. During the following week, only one member forgot the shoes. The timing mattered more than adding more words. The club kept the message itself unchanged during the test, so they could compare the effect of timing fairly.
passages.fullTranslation: テニス部は毎朝7時に練習の連絡を送っていました。それでも放課後の練習用の特別な靴を忘れる部員が何人もいました。部長は連絡文が短すぎると思いましたが、一人の生徒が、実際に何時に読まれているか調べようと提案しました。五日間、部員は連絡を開いた時刻を記録しました。多くの部員は登校前にはスマートフォンを見ず、昼ごろや授業後に読んでいました。その時間では家から靴を持ってくるには遅すぎます。部は連絡を前日の夜8時へ変更しました。次の一週間、靴を忘れたのは一人だけでした。言葉を増やすことより、送る時刻の方が重要だったのです。 比較を公平にするため、テスト中は連絡文そのものを変えず、送る時刻だけを変えました。

questions.prompt: What change most reduced the number of club members who forgot their shoes?
questions.answer: Sending the same reminder at eight o'clock the night before instead of seven in the morning.
questions.evidence: The club changed the reminder to eight o'clock the night before. During the following week, only one member forgot the shoes.
questions.evidenceJp: 部は連絡を前日の夜8時へ変更しました。次の一週間、靴を忘れたのは一人だけでした。
questions.reason: The club changed the timing while keeping the message itself the same, and forgetting decreased.

questions.prompt: When did most members actually read the morning reminder?
questions.answer: Around lunch or after classes.
questions.evidence: They read the message around lunch or after classes.
questions.evidenceJp: 多くの部員は登校前にはスマートフォンを見ず、昼ごろや授業後に読んでいました。
questions.reason: By then the members were already at school and could not easily get the shoes from home.

questions.prompt: Why did the seven-o'clock morning reminder often fail?
questions.answer: Because most members did not read it before school, and when they did read it the shoes were still at home.
questions.evidence: At that time, they were at school and the shoes were at home.
questions.evidenceJp: その時間では家から靴を持ってくるには遅すぎます。
questions.reason: A reminder only helps if it arrives and is read while the student can still act on it.

questions.prompt: What did club members record for five days?
questions.answer: The time when they opened the reminder.
questions.evidence: For five days, members recorded the time they opened the reminder.
questions.evidenceJp: 五日間、部員は連絡を開いた時刻を記録しました。
questions.reason: The records showed when the reminder was actually being seen.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: The club learned that the ____ of the reminder mattered more than adding more words.
questions.answer: timing
questions.evidence: The timing mattered more than adding more words.
questions.evidenceJp: 言葉を増やすことより、送る時刻の方が重要だったのです。
questions.reason: The successful change was when the same message was sent, not its length.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the club keep the wording of the reminder unchanged during the test?
questionSetB.answer: To make a fair comparison and isolate the effect of changing the sending time.
questionSetB.evidence: The club kept the message itself unchanged during the test, so they could compare the effect of timing fairly.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 比較を公平にするため、テスト中は連絡文そのものを変えず、送る時刻だけを変えました。
questionSetB.reason: If both wording and timing changed, the club could not tell which change caused the improvement.

questionSetB.prompt: What time did the club choose for the new reminder?
questionSetB.answer: Eight o'clock the night before.
questionSetB.evidence: The club changed the reminder to eight o'clock the night before.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 部は連絡を前日の夜8時へ変更しました。
questionSetB.reason: That gave members a chance to prepare the shoes while they were still at home.

questionSetB.prompt: How many members forgot the shoes during the week after the timing change?
questionSetB.answer: Only one member.
questionSetB.evidence: During the following week, only one member forgot the shoes.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 次の一週間、靴を忘れたのは一人だけでした。
questionSetB.reason: This result showed a large improvement compared with the earlier problem involving several members.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did one student suggest checking when members read the reminders?
questionSetB.answer: Because the problem might be when the message was seen rather than how short the message was.
questionSetB.evidence: The club leader thought the messages were too short, but one student suggested checking when members actually read them.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 部長は連絡文が短すぎると思いましたが、一人の生徒が、実際に何時に読まれているか調べようと提案しました。
questionSetB.reason: The suggestion tested an alternative explanation instead of assuming that message length was the cause.

questionSetB.prompt: What broader lesson can be drawn from the club's test?
questionSetB.answer: Information is more useful when it reaches people at a time when they can still act on it.
questionSetB.evidence: At that time, they were at school and the shoes were at home.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: その時間では家から靴を持ってくるには遅すぎます。
questionSetB.reason: The same reminder became more effective simply by being delivered before the members needed to leave home.

passages.title: Testing Two Hallway Routes
passages.body: Students at Midori Junior High wanted to reduce crowding between second and third period. There were two routes from the science rooms to the main classrooms. Route A was shorter by about thirty meters, so many students believed it was faster. A student team timed both routes for three days. When the halls were empty, Route A was faster. During class changes, however, students on Route A had to pass a narrow corner near the stairs. People from two directions met there and often stopped. Route B was longer but wider, and students could keep walking. The team also counted how many students reached the classroom within four minutes. Route B had the better result during busy times. Instead of telling everyone to avoid Route A, the school posted a suggestion: use Route B during class changes and Route A when the hall is quiet. The test showed that distance alone did not decide travel time. Teachers then repeated the timing test on a rainy day, when more students stayed inside. Route B still moved more steadily, which supported the recommendation.
passages.fullTranslation: みどり中学校の生徒たちは、2時間目と3時間目の間の混雑を減らしたいと考えました。理科室から普通教室へは二つの道がありました。Aルートは約30メートル短かったため、多くの生徒はそちらが速いと思っていました。生徒チームは三日間、両方の道にかかる時間を測りました。廊下が空いているときはAルートの方が速く着きました。しかし授業の移動時間には、Aルートでは階段近くの狭い角を通らなければなりません。二方向から来た人がそこで出会い、よく止まっていました。Bルートは長いものの幅が広く、生徒は歩き続けられました。チームは4分以内に教室へ着いた人数も数えました。混雑時はBルートの方がよい結果でした。学校は全員にAルートを使わないよう命じるのではなく、「授業の移動時はB、静かな時間はAを使う」という提案を掲示しました。調査から、距離だけでは移動時間は決まらないと分かりました。 先生たちは、生徒が廊下に多く残る雨の日にも時間を測り直しました。それでもBルートの流れは安定しており、提案を裏づける結果になりました。

questions.prompt: Why was Route B better during busy class changes even though it was longer?
questions.answer: Because it was wider, so students could keep moving instead of stopping at the narrow corner on Route A.
questions.evidence: Route B was longer but wider, and students could keep walking.
questions.evidenceJp: Bルートは長いものの幅が広く、生徒は歩き続けられました。
questions.reason: The wider route reduced the stopping caused by people meeting from two directions.

questions.prompt: About how much shorter was Route A?
questions.answer: About thirty meters.
questions.evidence: Route A was shorter by about thirty meters, so many students believed it was faster.
questions.evidenceJp: Aルートは約30メートル短かったため、多くの生徒はそちらが速いと思っていました。
questions.reason: The shorter distance was why many students initially expected Route A to be faster.

questions.prompt: Why did students often stop on Route A during class changes?
questions.answer: Because people coming from two directions met at a narrow corner near the stairs.
questions.evidence: People from two directions met there and often stopped.
questions.evidenceJp: 二方向から来た人がそこで出会い、よく止まっていました。
questions.reason: The narrow corner created congestion that offset Route A's shorter distance.

questions.prompt: When was Route A actually faster?
questions.answer: When the halls were empty.
questions.evidence: When the halls were empty, Route A was faster.
questions.evidenceJp: 廊下が空いているときはAルートの方が速く着きました。
questions.reason: Without crowding, the shorter distance gave Route A an advantage.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: The test showed that ____ alone did not decide travel time.

questions.evidence: The test showed that distance alone did not decide travel time.
questions.evidenceJp: 調査から、距離だけでは移動時間は決まらないと分かりました。
questions.reason: Crowding and route width also affected how quickly students could move.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the school recommend different routes for busy and quiet times instead of banning Route A?

questionSetB.evidence: The school posted a suggestion: use Route B during class changes and Route A when the hall is quiet.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 学校は全員にAルートを使わないよう命じるのではなく、「授業の移動時はB、静かな時間はAを使う」という提案を掲示しました。
questionSetB.reason: The test showed that the best route depended on conditions rather than one route always being better.

questionSetB.prompt: What additional measure did the team use besides timing the routes?
questionSetB.answer: They counted how many students reached the classroom within four minutes.
questionSetB.evidence: The team also counted how many students reached the classroom within four minutes.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: チームは4分以内に教室へ着いた人数も数えました。
questionSetB.reason: This gave another way to compare route performance during busy periods.

questionSetB.prompt: What happened when teachers repeated the test on a rainy day?

questionSetB.evidence: Route B still moved more steadily, which supported the recommendation.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: それでもBルートの流れは安定しており、提案を裏づける結果になりました。
questionSetB.reason: The repeated test supported the same conclusion under heavier indoor traffic.

questionSetB.prompt: Why was the rainy-day test useful?

questionSetB.reason: Repeating the test under different conditions checked whether the recommendation was reliable.

questionSetB.prompt: What broader lesson does this route test show?

passages.title: The Menu Board behind the Line
passages.body: At the school festival cafe, customers chose drinks at a menu board beside the counter. A long line formed even when the workers were ready. The class first planned to add another worker. Then Emi watched customers for ten minutes. She saw that people could not read the menu until they reached the front because the line itself blocked the board. Many customers began choosing only after the worker asked for an order. The class moved a copy of the menu to the entrance of the line. Customers decided while they waited, and the line moved more smoothly. No extra worker was needed. The class solved the delay by changing where information appeared. They measured the line again at the next busy hour and found that customers reached the counter with an order already chosen.
passages.fullTranslation: 文化祭のカフェでは、客はカウンター横のメニューボードを見て飲み物を選びました。係の人が準備できていても長い列ができました。クラスは最初、係を一人増やそうと考えました。しかしエミが10分間客の様子を観察すると、列そのものがメニューを隠し、先頭に来るまで読めないことに気づきました。多くの客は係に注文を聞かれてから初めて選び始めていました。クラスはメニューの写しを列の入口へ移しました。客は待っている間に選べるようになり、列はよりスムーズに進みました。係を増やす必要はありませんでした。情報を見せる場所を変えることで遅れを解決したのです。 次の混雑時間にも列を測ると、多くの客が注文を決めた状態でカウンターへ着くようになっていました。

questions.prompt: What was the real cause of the long line at the festival cafe?
questions.answer: Customers could not see the menu early enough to choose before reaching the counter.
questions.evidence: She saw that people could not read the menu until they reached the front because the line itself blocked the board.
questions.evidenceJp: しかしエミが10分間客の様子を観察すると、列そのものがメニューを隠し、先頭に来るまで読めないことに気づきました。
questions.reason: The workers were ready, but customers delayed ordering because the information was visible too late.

questions.prompt: What did the class first plan to do about the long line?
questions.answer: Add another worker.
questions.evidence: The class first planned to add another worker.
questions.evidenceJp: クラスは最初、係を一人増やそうと考えました。
questions.reason: The class initially assumed the delay came from insufficient staffing.

questions.prompt: Why did moving a menu copy to the entrance help?
questions.answer: Customers could decide what to order while waiting instead of waiting until they reached the counter.
questions.evidence: Customers decided while they waited, and the line moved more smoothly.
questions.evidenceJp: 客は待っている間に選べるようになり、列はよりスムーズに進みました。
questions.reason: The change moved decision-making earlier in the process.

questions.prompt: Did the cafe need an extra worker after changing the menu location?
questions.answer: No.
questions.evidence: No extra worker was needed.
questions.evidenceJp: 係を増やす必要はありませんでした。
questions.reason: Improving access to information solved the delay without increasing staff.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: The class solved the delay by changing where ____ appeared.
questions.answer: information
questions.evidence: The class solved the delay by changing where information appeared.
questions.evidenceJp: 情報を見せる場所を変えることで遅れを解決したのです。
questions.reason: The key intervention was relocating the menu information, not adding labor.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did Emi watch customers before the class added another worker?
questionSetB.answer: To find out where the delay actually occurred instead of assuming the workers were the problem.
questionSetB.evidence: Then Emi watched customers for ten minutes.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: しかしエミが10分間客の様子を観察すると、列そのものがメニューを隠し、先頭に来るまで読めないことに気づきました。
questionSetB.reason: Observation revealed that customers, not workers, were waiting to make choices.

questionSetB.prompt: When did many customers begin choosing a drink before the change?
questionSetB.answer: Only after a worker asked for their order.
questionSetB.evidence: Many customers began choosing only after the worker asked for an order.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 多くの客は係に注文を聞かれてから初めて選び始めていました。
questionSetB.reason: This late decision point slowed the line at the counter.

questionSetB.prompt: What did the class find when it measured the line again at the next busy hour?
questionSetB.answer: Customers were reaching the counter with their orders already chosen.
questionSetB.evidence: They measured the line again at the next busy hour and found that customers reached the counter with an order already chosen.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 次の混雑時間にも列を測ると、多くの客が注文を決めた状態でカウンターへ着くようになっていました。
questionSetB.reason: The follow-up measurement showed that the menu move changed customer behavior as intended.

questionSetB.prompt: What does 'blocked' mean when the passage says the line blocked the board?
questionSetB.answer: Prevented people behind the line from seeing the menu board clearly.
questionSetB.evidence: She saw that people could not read the menu until they reached the front because the line itself blocked the board.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: しかしエミが10分間客の様子を観察すると、列そのものがメニューを隠し、先頭に来るまで読めないことに気づきました。
questionSetB.reason: The people in the line physically interfered with visibility of the menu.

questionSetB.prompt: What general lesson can be learned from the cafe's solution?
questionSetB.answer: A process can become faster by placing needed information where people can use it before they reach the decision point.
questionSetB.evidence: Customers decided while they waited, and the line moved more smoothly.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 客は待っている間に選べるようになり、列はよりスムーズに進みました。
questionSetB.reason: Earlier access to the menu removed waiting at the counter without requiring more staff.

passages.title: Two Versions of the Club Form
passages.body: The cooking club used both a paper form and an online form for new members. The online form had more unanswered entries, so the club thought students disliked using phones. Riku compared the two forms carefully. The paper version asked for a name, class, and contact choice. The online version also asked, “What dish do you most want to make?” before students could finish. Some first-year students did not know what to write and stopped there. The club made that question optional and moved it to the end. After the change, almost everyone completed the online form. The problem was not the device; one required question was creating the difficulty. They kept both forms available, because some students still preferred paper even after the online form became easier.
passages.fullTranslation: 料理部は新入部員向けに紙の申込書とオンライン申込書の両方を使っていました。オンラインの方は未記入のものが多く、部員は生徒がスマートフォンで入力するのを嫌っているのだと思いました。リクが二つをよく比べると、紙は名前・クラス・連絡方法だけを尋ねていました。一方オンライン版では、最後まで進む前に「いちばん作ってみたい料理は何ですか」と答える必要がありました。何を書けばよいか分からず、そこで止まる一年生がいました。部はその質問を任意にし、最後へ移しました。変更後はほとんどの生徒がオンライン申込書を最後まで書けました。問題は端末ではなく、一つの必須質問だったのです。 オンライン版が使いやすくなった後も紙を好む生徒はいたため、部は二つの申込方法を残しました。

passages.title: The Sidewalk after the Snow Melted
passages.body: After a light snowfall, students checked two walking routes from the station to school. Route A ran beside tall buildings, while Route B followed an open street. Route A was shorter, and teachers usually recommended it. By noon, most snow had melted, but several students reported slipping on Route A the next morning. The safety committee visited both routes at eight o'clock. Route B was wet but clear. On Route A, a shaded section still had thin ice because sunlight did not reach the ground early in the day. The committee returned at noon and found that the ice was gone. Instead of saying Route A was always dangerous, they changed the winter notice. It recommended Route B on cold mornings after snow and allowed either route later when conditions were clear. They also marked the shaded section on a map. Their decision used both place and time, not just the total distance. The committee asked students to report new icy spots for two weeks. No additional place caused repeated problems, so the map stayed focused on the shaded section.
passages.fullTranslation: 少し雪が降った後、生徒たちは駅から学校までの二つの徒歩ルートを確認しました。Aルートは高い建物のそばを通り、Bルートは開けた通りを進みます。Aの方が短く、先生たちは普段Aを勧めていました。昼までにはほとんどの雪が解けましたが、翌朝Aルートで滑ったという生徒が何人かいました。安全委員会は朝8時に両方の道を見に行きました。Bはぬれていましたが、歩ける状態でした。Aでは、朝早く日光が地面に届かない日陰の部分に薄い氷が残っていました。委員会が正午にもう一度行くと氷はなくなっていました。そこで「Aはいつも危険」とするのではなく、冬の案内を変えました。雪の後の寒い朝はBを勧め、後の時間に安全ならどちらも使えるようにしました。地図には日陰の場所も示しました。判断には距離だけでなく、場所と時間の両方が使われました。 委員会は二週間、新しい凍結場所があれば報告するよう生徒に頼みました。繰り返し問題になる別の場所はなく、地図では日陰の区間を重点的に示しました。

sentences: After a light snowfall,
students checked two walking routes
from the station to school.
Route A ran beside tall buildings,
while Route B followed an open street.
Route A was shorter,
and teachers usually recommended it.
By noon,
most snow had melted,
but several students reported slipping on Route A
the next morning.
The safety committee visited both routes
at eight o'clock.
Route B was wet but clear.
On Route A,
a shaded section still had thin ice
because sunlight did not reach the ground
early in the day.
The committee returned at noon
and found
that the ice was gone.
Instead of saying Route A was always dangerous,
they changed the winter notice.
It recommended Route B
on cold mornings after snow
and allowed either route later
when conditions were clear.
They also marked the shaded section
on a map.
Their decision used both place and time,
not just the total distance.
The committee asked students
to report new icy spots
for two weeks.
No additional place caused repeated problems,
so the map stayed focused
on the shaded section.

questions.prompt: Why did the committee change its winter route advice?
questions.answer: Because Route A could be icy on cold mornings after snow even though it was usually shorter.
questions.evidence: On Route A, a shaded section still had thin ice because sunlight did not reach the ground early in the day.
questions.evidenceJp: Aでは、朝早く日光が地面に届かない日陰の部分に薄い氷が残っていました。
questions.reason: The morning condition of the shaded section made the usual shorter route less safe at that time.

questions.prompt: What did the committee find when it returned to Route A at noon?
questions.answer: The ice had disappeared.
questions.evidence: The committee returned at noon and found that the ice was gone.
questions.evidenceJp: 委員会が正午にもう一度行くと氷はなくなっていました。
questions.reason: This showed that the danger changed with time of day.

questions.prompt: Why did the committee avoid saying Route A was always dangerous?
questions.answer: Because the ice was present in the cold morning but gone by noon.
questions.evidence: Instead of saying Route A was always dangerous, they changed the winter notice.
questions.evidenceJp: そこで「Aはいつも危険」とするのではなく、冬の案内を変えました。
questions.reason: The evidence showed a time-specific risk rather than a permanent condition.

questions.prompt: What did the new winter notice recommend?
questions.answer: Use Route B on cold mornings after snow and allow either route later when conditions are clear.
questions.evidence: It recommended Route B on cold mornings after snow and allowed either route later when conditions were clear.
questions.evidenceJp: 雪の後の寒い朝はBを勧め、後の時間に安全ならどちらも使えるようにしました。
questions.reason: The advice combined weather, time, and actual route conditions.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: The committee's decision used both ____ and time, not only distance.
questions.answer: place
questions.evidence: Their decision used both place and time, not just the total distance.
questions.evidenceJp: 判断には距離だけでなく、場所と時間の両方が使われました。
questions.reason: The shaded location and the morning timing together explained the risk.

questionSetB.prompt: What does the comparison between Route A at eight o'clock and at noon show?
questionSetB.answer: A route's safety can change during the same day.
questionSetB.evidence: The committee returned at noon and found that the ice was gone.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 委員会が正午にもう一度行くと氷はなくなっていました。
questionSetB.reason: The same shaded section was icy earlier but clear later.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the committee mark the shaded section on a map?
questionSetB.answer: To show students the specific place where morning ice repeatedly remained.
questionSetB.evidence: They also marked the shaded section on a map.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 地図には日陰の場所も示しました。
questionSetB.reason: The risk was tied to a particular part of Route A rather than the whole route.

questionSetB.prompt: What did the two-week follow-up reports show?
questionSetB.answer: No other location repeatedly caused the same problem.
questionSetB.evidence: No additional place caused repeated problems, so the map stayed focused on the shaded section.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 繰り返し問題になる別の場所はなく、地図では日陰の区間を重点的に示しました。
questionSetB.reason: The follow-up supported keeping the warning focused on the known shaded area.

questionSetB.prompt: In the passage, what does “shaded” describe?
questionSetB.answer: An area that receives little or no sunlight.
questionSetB.evidence: On Route A, a shaded section still had thin ice because sunlight did not reach the ground early in the day.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: Aでは、朝早く日光が地面に届かない日陰の部分に薄い氷が残っていました。
questionSetB.reason: The explanation directly connects the shaded condition with lack of early sunlight.

questionSetB.prompt: What is the main lesson of the committee's investigation?
questionSetB.answer: Safety advice should reflect when and where a problem occurs instead of relying on one simple measure such as distance.
questionSetB.evidence: Their decision used both place and time, not just the total distance.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 判断には距離だけでなく、場所と時間の両方が使われました。
questionSetB.reason: The final advice was based on specific conditions rather than a single fixed judgment about the route.

passages.title: Why Students Skipped the Second Shelf
passages.body: The school library created a shelf for short English books. The first shelf was used often, but the second shelf stayed almost full. The librarian thought the books on the second shelf were too difficult. A student team watched readers and asked a few questions. They learned that many students did not realize the second shelf was part of the same collection. Its category card was placed low behind a row of books. The team moved the card to eye level and added the same symbol used on the first shelf. During the next two weeks, more books from the second shelf were borrowed. The books had not changed; the way the shelf was labeled had.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校図書館は短い英語の本を集めた棚を作りました。一段目の本はよく借りられましたが、二段目はほとんど本が残ったままでした。司書は二段目の本が難しすぎるのだと思いました。生徒チームが利用者を観察し、何人かに質問すると、多くの生徒が二段目も同じコーナーだと気づいていないことが分かりました。分類カードが本の列の後ろの低い位置に隠れていたのです。チームはカードを目の高さへ移し、一段目と同じ記号を加えました。次の二週間で二段目の本も多く借りられました。本そのものではなく、棚の示し方が変わったのです。

questions.prompt: What was the real reason students used the second shelf less often?
questions.answer: Many students did not realize it belonged to the same English-book collection.
questions.evidence: They learned that many students did not realize the second shelf was part of the same collection.

questions.evidence: Its category card was placed low behind a row of books.
questions.evidenceJp: 分類カードが本の列の後ろの低い位置に隠れていたのです。
questions.reason: Its position made the connection between the two shelves hard to notice.

questions.prompt: Why did the team add the same symbol used on the first shelf?

questions.evidence: The team moved the card to eye level and added the same symbol used on the first shelf.

questions.reason: Matching visual signals helped readers connect the second shelf with the first.

questions.prompt: What changed during the two weeks after the labeling was improved?
questions.answer: More books from the second shelf were borrowed.
questions.evidence: During the next two weeks, more books from the second shelf were borrowed.
questions.evidenceJp: 次の二週間で二段目の本も多く借りられました。
questions.reason: Borrowing increased after the shelf became easier to identify.

questions.evidenceJp: 本そのものではなく、棚の示し方が変わったのです。
questions.reason: The final sentence identifies presentation, not book difficulty, as the changed factor.

questionSetB.prompt: Why was the librarian's first explanation probably wrong?
questionSetB.answer: Because borrowing rose after only the label and symbol were changed, while the books stayed the same.
questionSetB.evidence: The books had not changed; the way the shelf was labeled had.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 本そのものではなく、棚の示し方が変わったのです。
questionSetB.reason: If difficulty were the main problem, changing only the label would not be expected to improve borrowing so clearly.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the student team watch readers and ask questions?
questionSetB.answer: To find out why the second shelf was being overlooked instead of relying on an assumption.
questionSetB.evidence: A student team watched readers and asked a few questions.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 生徒チームが利用者を観察し、何人かに質問すると、多くの生徒が二段目も同じコーナーだと気づいていないことが分かりました。
questionSetB.reason: Observation and questions provided evidence about what readers actually noticed.

questionSetB.prompt: What does “eye level” mean in this passage?
questionSetB.answer: A height where people can easily see the card while looking normally.
questionSetB.evidence: The team moved the card to eye level and added the same symbol used on the first shelf.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: チームはカードを目の高さへ移し、一段目と同じ記号を加えました。
questionSetB.reason: Moving the card higher made it easier for readers to notice.

questionSetB.prompt: Which statement is supported by the passage?
questionSetB.answer: A small change in how information is displayed can change how people use a resource.
questionSetB.evidence: During the next two weeks, more books from the second shelf were borrowed.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 次の二週間で二段目の本も多く借りられました。
questionSetB.reason: Borrowing changed after the visual labeling changed.

questionSetB.prompt: What lesson did the shelf experiment demonstrate?
questionSetB.answer: Before changing the resource itself, check whether people can clearly recognize and understand how it is organized.
questionSetB.evidence: They learned that many students did not realize the second shelf was part of the same collection.

questionSetB.reason: The problem came from recognition and labeling, not from the books themselves.

passages.title: The Announcement with Too Much Music
passages.body: The broadcasting club made a lunchtime announcement about a school clean-up day. They added cheerful background music because they wanted students to listen. After the announcement, many students remembered the event but could not say where to meet. The club tested the recording with twelve students. When the music was loud, several missed the meeting place and start time. With softer music, almost all of them understood those details. The club kept the same words and the same short song but lowered the music during important information. The next announcement was easier to follow. The test showed that attractive sound should not hide the message it is meant to support. A short follow-up survey also showed that students still noticed the cheerful music, even at the lower volume.
passages.fullTranslation: 放送部は昼休みに校内清掃の日についての放送を作りました。生徒に聞いてもらうため、明るい背景音楽を付けました。放送後、多くの生徒は行事があることは覚えていましたが、集合場所を言えませんでした。部員は12人の生徒に録音を聞いてもらいました。音楽が大きいと、集合場所や開始時刻を聞き逃す人が何人もいました。音楽を小さくすると、ほとんどの人がその情報を理解できました。部は言葉も短い曲も変えず、大切な情報のところだけ音楽を下げました。次の放送は聞き取りやすくなりました。人を引きつける音も、支えるはずの内容を隠してはいけないと分かりました。 短い追加アンケートでは、音量を下げても生徒たちは明るい音楽に気づいていたことも分かりました。

questions.prompt: What problem did the broadcasting club find in its first announcement?

questions.prompt: How many students listened to the test recording?

questions.prompt: Why did the club keep the same words and the same short song during the change?

questions.prompt: What happened when the music was made softer?

questions.evidenceJp: 音楽を小さくすると、ほとんどの人がその情報を理解できました。
questions.reason: Lowering the background volume improved comprehension.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: Attractive sound should support a message, not ____ it.
questions.answer: hide
questions.evidence: The test showed that attractive sound should not hide the message it is meant to support.
questions.evidenceJp: 人を引きつける音も、支えるはずの内容を隠してはいけないと分かりました。
questions.reason: This sentence states the main lesson of the test.

questionSetB.prompt: Why was it useful that students still noticed the music after its volume was lowered?

questionSetB.evidence: A short follow-up survey also showed that students still noticed the cheerful music, even at the lower volume.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 短い追加アンケートでは、音量を下げても生徒たちは明るい音楽に気づいていたことも分かりました。
questionSetB.reason: The quieter music still attracted attention while allowing the message to be understood.

questionSetB.prompt: Why was remembering only that the event existed not enough?
questionSetB.answer: Students also needed the meeting place and start time to take part correctly.
questionSetB.evidence: After the announcement, many students remembered the event but could not say where to meet.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 放送後、多くの生徒は行事があることは覚えていましたが、集合場所を言えませんでした。
questionSetB.reason: An announcement is useful only if listeners understand the action details as well as the event itself.

questionSetB.prompt: What does “follow” mean in “The next announcement was easier to follow”?
questionSetB.answer: To understand as it is heard.
questionSetB.evidence: The next announcement was easier to follow.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 次の放送は聞き取りやすくなりました。
questionSetB.reason: The sentence describes improved understanding, not physically following someone.

questionSetB.prompt: Which statement best matches the club's test?

questionSetB.evidence: The club kept the same words and the same short song but lowered the music during important information.

questionSetB.reason: The test isolated how loud the background music was during key information.

questionSetB.prompt: What broader principle can be learned from the club's experiment?
questionSetB.answer: Design elements that attract attention should never interfere with the information people need to understand.

passages.title: The Fast Checkout That Started Late
passages.body: At the school festival shop, Class 2-1 used two checkout tables. Table A served each customer quickly, but its line often became long. Table B served people a little more slowly, yet its line disappeared sooner. The class first thought Table A needed another cashier. Mika watched the beginning of each sale period and found a different problem. Workers at Table A started setting out bags and change only after customers were already waiting. For the first five minutes, one cashier prepared supplies instead of serving people. Table B prepared everything ten minutes before opening. The class changed the setup order at Table A. Bags, coins, and price sheets were ready before the next sale period. The service speed for each customer did not change, but the early line became much shorter. The students learned that a fast process can still create a long wait if preparation begins too late. They improved the work before the first customer arrived. They repeated the change during the final sale period and saw the same pattern, so the improvement was not limited to one unusually quiet moment.
passages.fullTranslation: 文化祭の店で2年1組は二つの会計台を使いました。A台は一人ひとりの会計は速いのに、列が長くなりがちでした。B台は少し時間がかかりましたが、列は早くなくなりました。クラスは最初、A台に会計係をもう一人増やす必要があると思いました。ミカが販売開始時を観察すると、別の問題が分かりました。A台では客がすでに待ってから袋やおつりを準備し始めていました。最初の5分間、一人の係は接客せず準備をしていたのです。B台では開店10分前にすべて準備していました。クラスはA台の準備の順番を変えました。次の販売時間には袋・小銭・価格表を事前にそろえました。一人の客にかかる会計時間は変わりませんでしたが、最初の列はずっと短くなりました。作業そのものが速くても、準備開始が遅ければ長い待ち時間が生まれると分かりました。最初の客が来る前の仕事を改善したのです。 最後の販売時間にも同じ変更を繰り返すと同じ傾向が見られたため、たまたま空いていた一回だけの改善ではないと確認できました。

questions.prompt: Why did Table A develop a long line even though it served each customer quickly?
questions.answer: Because part of the staff prepared bags and change only after customers had already begun waiting.
questions.evidence: Workers at Table A started setting out bags and change only after customers were already waiting.
questions.evidenceJp: A台では客がすでに待ってから袋やおつりを準備し始めていました。
questions.reason: Late preparation reduced the number of workers serving customers at the beginning of the sale period.

questions.prompt: How was Table B prepared differently from Table A?
questions.answer: Table B had everything ready ten minutes before opening.
questions.evidence: Table B prepared everything ten minutes before opening.
questions.evidenceJp: B台では開店10分前にすべて準備していました。
questions.reason: The preparation was completed before customers arrived.

questions.prompt: Why did the class change the setup order instead of immediately adding another cashier?
questions.answer: Because Mika found that late preparation, not slow individual service, was creating the early line.
questions.evidence: Mika watched the beginning of each sale period and found a different problem.
questions.evidenceJp: ミカが販売開始時を観察すると、別の問題が分かりました。
questions.reason: The observation identified a process problem that could be fixed without increasing staff.

questions.prompt: What changed after bags, coins, and price sheets were prepared before the sale?
questions.answer: The early line became much shorter even though service time per customer stayed the same.
questions.evidence: The service speed for each customer did not change, but the early line became much shorter.
questions.evidenceJp: 一人の客にかかる会計時間は変わりませんでしたが、最初の列はずっと短くなりました。
questions.reason: Earlier preparation improved the flow before individual checkout speed changed.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: A process can be fast but still create a long wait when ____ begins too late.
questions.answer: preparation
questions.evidence: The students learned that a fast process can still create a long wait if preparation begins too late.
questions.evidenceJp: 作業そのものが速くても、準備開始が遅ければ長い待ち時間が生まれると分かりました。
questions.reason: This sentence states the main lesson from the checkout experiment.

questionSetB.prompt: What does the repeated result in the final sale period suggest?
questionSetB.answer: The shorter line was likely caused by the preparation change rather than by one unusually quiet period.
questionSetB.evidence: They repeated the change during the final sale period and saw the same pattern, so the improvement was not limited to one unusually quiet moment.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 最後の販売時間にも同じ変更を繰り返すと同じ傾向が見られたため、たまたま空いていた一回だけの改善ではないと確認できました。
questionSetB.reason: Repeating the result gives stronger evidence that the process change mattered.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the first five minutes matter so much at Table A?
questionSetB.answer: One cashier was preparing supplies instead of serving the customers who were already waiting.
questionSetB.evidence: For the first five minutes, one cashier prepared supplies instead of serving people.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 最初の5分間、一人の係は接客せず準備をしていたのです。
questionSetB.reason: That reduced checkout capacity exactly when the first line was forming.

questionSetB.prompt: What does “setup order” mean in this passage?
questionSetB.answer: The sequence in which the workers prepared the checkout area and began serving customers.
questionSetB.evidence: The class changed the setup order at Table A.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: クラスはA台の準備の順番を変えました。
questionSetB.reason: The class moved supply preparation to before the sale period instead of doing it after customers arrived.

questionSetB.prompt: Which statement is supported by the passage?
questionSetB.answer: Improving work before the first customer arrived reduced waiting without making each checkout faster.
questionSetB.evidence: They improved the work before the first customer arrived.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 最初の客が来る前の仕事を改善したのです。
questionSetB.reason: The intervention targeted preparation timing rather than the speed of serving each customer.

questionSetB.prompt: What broader lesson does the checkout example show?
questionSetB.answer: To understand a waiting problem, examine the whole process including what happens before service begins.
questionSetB.evidence: The students learned that a fast process can still create a long wait if preparation begins too late.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 作業そのものが速くても、準備開始が遅ければ長い待ち時間が生まれると分かりました。
questionSetB.reason: The class solved the problem by looking beyond the visible speed of individual checkouts.

passages.title: The Direction Sign beside the Tree
passages.body: Visitors to the school open day often asked where the gym was, even though a direction sign stood near the front gate. The student council first planned to make the letters larger. Before printing a new sign, they watched arriving families. From the gate, part of the sign was hidden by leaves from a small tree. People walking from the parking area could see it, but people from the station could not. The council moved the sign two meters to the left and tested it again from both directions. More visitors found the gym without asking. The original words were clear; the sign simply needed to be visible from the main approach. They left the tree in place and checked the sign again one week later to make sure new leaf growth had not hidden it.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校公開日に来た人たちは、正門近くに案内板があるのに、よく体育館の場所を尋ねていました。生徒会は最初、文字を大きくしようと考えました。新しい案内を印刷する前に、来校者の様子を観察しました。正門から見ると、小さな木の葉が案内板の一部を隠していました。駐車場から来る人には見えましたが、駅から歩いてくる人には見えませんでした。生徒会は案内板を左へ2メートル移し、両方の方向からもう一度確かめました。すると尋ねなくても体育館を見つける来校者が増えました。元の言葉は分かりやすく、主な来校方向から見える場所に置く必要があったのです。 木はそのまま残し、一週間後にも葉が伸びて再び案内を隠していないか確認しました。

passages.title: Five Quiet Minutes before Practice
passages.body: The basketball team often lost practice time because players stopped to look for balls, towels, or water after practice began. The captain suggested making practice fifteen minutes longer. Another student asked the team to test a smaller change first. For one week, everyone spent five quiet minutes before practice checking equipment and filling water bottles. The team recorded how often practice stopped later. The number of interruptions fell from an average of six to two. Players finished the planned drills without staying later. The team kept the five-minute check. They gained useful practice time by organizing the start, not by extending the end. The five minutes also gave injured players time to tell the captain what activities they needed to avoid that day.
passages.fullTranslation: バスケットボール部では、練習が始まってからボールやタオル、水を探すために止まり、時間を失うことがよくありました。主将は練習を15分延ばそうと提案しました。別の生徒は、その前にもっと小さな変更を試そうと言いました。一週間、全員が練習前の5分間を静かな準備時間にし、用具確認と水筒の準備をしました。その後、練習中に何回止まったか記録すると、平均6回から2回へ減りました。遅くまで残らず予定した練習を終えられました。部は5分間の確認を続けることにしました。終わりを延ばすのではなく、始まりを整えることで使える練習時間を増やしたのです。 その5分間は、けがをしている選手がその日に避ける活動を主将へ伝える時間にもなりました。

passages.title: The Book Drive with Too Many Rules
passages.body: A student group collected used books for a community reading room. Their first poster listed seven rules about accepted books. Even so, many donated books had to be returned. The students thought people had ignored the poster. They examined thirty rejected books and asked five donors what had confused them. Several donors had read the rules but did not understand phrases such as “good condition” and “recent reference material.” The group made a new poster with three main rules and pictures of examples. It showed a clean storybook as acceptable, a book with missing pages as unacceptable, and school reference books from the last five years as acceptable. They kept the detailed rules on a smaller sheet for volunteers. During the next collection, fewer books were rejected, and donors asked fewer questions. The students did not simply make the rules shorter. They separated information people needed before donating from details volunteers needed while checking books. Volunteers recorded the reasons for every rejected book during the second collection. Water damage, not unclear categories, became the most common reason after the redesign.
passages.fullTranslation: 生徒グループは地域の読書室のために中古本を集めました。最初のポスターには受け入れられる本について七つの規則が書かれていました。それでも寄付された本の多くを返さなければなりませんでした。生徒たちは、みんながポスターを読んでいないのだと思いました。そこで返却した30冊を調べ、寄付した5人に何が分かりにくかったか尋ねました。規則は読んでいても、「よい状態」や「新しい参考資料」といった表現の意味が分からない人がいました。グループは主な規則を三つにし、例の写真を付けた新しいポスターを作りました。きれいな物語の本は受け入れ可、ページがない本は不可、学校用参考書は過去5年のものなら可と示しました。細かな規則は係用の小さな紙に残しました。次の回収では返却する本が減り、質問も少なくなりました。ただ短くしたのではなく、寄付前に必要な情報と、係が本を確認するときに必要な詳細を分けたのです。 二回目の回収では、係が返却理由をすべて記録しました。案内改善後は、分類の分かりにくさではなく水ぬれが最も多い返却理由になりました。

passages.title: The Entrance That Visitors Passed
passages.body: A community study room opened on Saturdays, but first-time visitors often walked past its entrance. The door looked like a staff door and stayed closed to keep the room quiet. Students helping there watched the hallway and spoke with visitors. They found that a small “Study Room” label was easy to miss, especially from the stairs. The students added a welcome sign at eye level and placed a small open sign beside the handle when the room was available. They did not leave the door open because noise would enter. The next Saturday, more visitors entered without asking for help. Clear signs made the entrance feel public while the room stayed quiet. They also placed the opening hours below the welcome sign, which prevented people from trying the door after the room had closed.
passages.fullTranslation: 地域の学習室は土曜日に開いていましたが、初めて来た人は入口を通り過ぎることがよくありました。ドアは職員用のように見え、室内を静かにするため閉じたままでした。手伝っていた生徒たちは廊下を観察し、来訪者にも話を聞きました。小さな「学習室」という表示は、特に階段側から来ると見落としやすいと分かりました。生徒たちは目の高さに歓迎の案内を付け、利用できる時間には取っ手の横に小さな「開室中」の表示を置きました。騒音が入るのでドア自体は開けっぱなしにしませんでした。次の土曜日には、助けを求めず入れる人が増えました。分かりやすい表示によって、静けさを保ちながら公共の入口だと伝えられました。 歓迎表示の下には利用時間も付け、閉室後にドアを開けようとする人が出ないようにしました。

passages.title: A Study Plan That Needed One Change
passages.body: There were four students with the same two-hour study plan before a test. They began with easy review, then did difficult math, and finished with vocabulary. After three days, they compared concentration notes. All four felt most tired during math, which began after seventy minutes. They first considered adding another study hour. Instead, they moved math to the first forty minutes and put easy review later. The total study time stayed two hours. During the next three days, the students completed more math problems and made fewer careless mistakes. They learned that changing the order of tasks could help more than simply making the plan longer. The students kept the same breaks and subjects, allowing them to judge the effect of task order instead of several changes at once.
passages.fullTranslation: 四人の生徒がテスト前に同じ2時間の勉強計画を作りました。最初に簡単な復習をし、その後に難しい数学、最後に単語学習をしました。三日後、集中についての記録を比べると、四人とも70分ほどたって始まる数学の時間に最も疲れていました。最初は勉強をもう1時間増やそうと考えましたが、数学を最初の40分へ移し、簡単な復習を後へ回しました。勉強時間は2時間のままです。次の三日間では、解けた数学の問題が増え、不注意なミスも減りました。計画をただ長くするより、課題の順番を変える方が役立つことが分かりました。 休憩や学習科目は同じにし、複数の条件を一度に変えず課題の順番の効果を確かめました。

passages.title: The Reusable Plate Trial
passages.body: The school festival wanted to reduce trash from food stalls. One class suggested using reusable plates everywhere, while another worried about washing time. The planning team ran a small trial at three stalls. At the curry stall, most customers ate near the return station, and 92 percent of plates came back quickly. At the snack stall near the field, many customers walked away while eating, and only 61 percent returned plates to the correct place. The dessert stall had a good return rate but created a long washing line during one busy hour. The team decided not to use one system for every stall. They chose reusable plates for curry, improved the washing schedule for dessert, and kept paper containers at the field snack stall while adding a recycling box. The plan reduced waste without creating a plate shortage. The trial showed that a useful environmental idea still needed to fit how each stall actually worked. The team posted simple return instructions at the two reusable-plate stalls and counted missing plates at closing time. Only a few were unreturned, so the next event kept the mixed system.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校祭では、食べ物の店から出るごみを減らしたいと考えました。あるクラスはすべての店で繰り返し使える皿を使おうと提案し、別のクラスは洗う時間を心配しました。計画チームは三つの店で小さな実験をしました。カレー店では、多くの客が返却場所の近くで食べ、92パーセントの皿がすぐ戻りました。運動場近くの軽食店では、食べながら移動する客が多く、正しい場所へ返された皿は61パーセントでした。デザート店は返却率はよかったものの、混雑する1時間に洗い物の列が長くなりました。チームは全店を同じ方式にしませんでした。カレーは再利用皿、デザートは洗浄予定を改善し、運動場の軽食店は紙容器を残しながらリサイクル箱を加えました。皿不足を起こさず、ごみを減らせる計画になりました。環境によい考えでも、各店の実際の使われ方に合わせる必要があると分かりました。 チームは再利用皿を使う二店に簡単な返却案内を出し、閉店時に不足枚数も数えました。戻らなかった皿はわずかだったため、次の行事でも混合方式を続けることになりました。

passages.title: The Speaker near the Courtyard
passages.body: The school tested emergency announcements in four areas. Students in the library, gym, and east hall heard every sentence clearly. In the courtyard, several students understood only parts of the message. The sound was loud enough, so the committee first suspected the students were talking. A second test was done when the courtyard was quiet. The same words were still hard to hear near one wall because the sound from a speaker returned as an echo. The school turned that speaker slightly toward the open area and tested again. The message became clearer without increasing the volume. The problem came from direction and echo, not because the sound was quiet. A final test included a spoken room number and a short safety instruction. Students in all four areas could repeat both correctly.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校は四つの場所で緊急放送の聞こえ方を調べました。図書室、体育館、東廊下ではすべての文がはっきり聞こえました。中庭では、内容の一部しか分からない生徒が何人かいました。音量は十分だったため、委員会は最初、生徒のおしゃべりが原因だと思いました。中庭が静かなときにもう一度試しても、ある壁の近くでは同じ言葉が聞き取りにくいままでした。スピーカーの音が壁から返り、響いていたのです。学校はそのスピーカーを少し開けた場所の方へ向け、再び試しました。音量を上げなくても放送は聞き取りやすくなりました。問題は音の弱さではなく、向きと反響でした。 最終テストでは部屋番号と短い安全指示も放送し、四つの場所すべてで生徒が両方を正しく言い直せました。

questions.prompt: What caused the courtyard announcement problem?

questions.prompt: Why did the second quiet-courtyard test matter?

questions.prompt: What change made the courtyard message clearer?

questions.reason: The solution changed speaker direction rather than loudness.

questionSetB.prompt: Why was increasing the volume unlikely to solve the original problem?

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the school include a room number and a safety instruction in the final test?

questionSetB.prompt: What does “echo” mean in this passage?

passages.title: The Survey with a Long First Page
passages.body: The student council made an online survey about the school cafeteria. Many students opened it, but fewer than half reached the main food questions. The council first thought students were not interested in lunch. Then they checked where people stopped. The first page asked for grade, club, usual lunch place, and several optional comments before the cafeteria questions began. Younger students often left during that page. The council kept only grade and usual lunch place at the start and moved the other questions to the end. In the next survey, far more students reached the food section. The council improved completion by shortening the path to the questions that mattered most. They also displayed a progress bar, so students could see that the remaining questions were short after the main section.
passages.fullTranslation: 生徒会は学校の食堂についてオンラインアンケートを作りました。多くの生徒が開きましたが、中心となる食べ物の質問まで進んだのは半分以下でした。生徒会は最初、昼食に興味がないのだと思いました。しかしどこで回答をやめたか調べると、最初のページに学年・部活動・普段昼食を食べる場所・いくつかの任意コメント欄があり、その後に食堂の質問が始まる構成でした。低学年の生徒はそのページでやめることが多くありました。生徒会は最初を学年と普段の昼食場所だけにし、ほかの質問を最後へ移しました。次のアンケートでは、ずっと多くの生徒が食べ物の質問まで進みました。いちばん重要な質問までの道のりを短くすることで回答率を改善しました。 さらに進行状況の表示を付け、中心部分の後に残る質問が少ないことも生徒に分かるようにしました。

passages.title: The Community Pantry Temperature Log
passages.body: A community pantry stored milk and prepared food in two refrigerators. Volunteers noticed that food from Refrigerator B was sometimes thrown away before its use-by date because the temperature record showed short rises above the target range. Some people wanted to replace the refrigerator immediately. A group of students examined one month of temperature logs together with delivery times. Most rises happened between 4:00 and 4:30 p.m., when several boxes were delivered and the door stayed open while volunteers sorted food. On days without a large delivery, the temperature remained stable. The students tested a new process: boxes were sorted on a table first, and the refrigerator door was opened only when items were ready to be placed inside. The next week's log showed smaller and shorter temperature rises. A technician still checked the refrigerator and found no mechanical problem. The pantry kept the refrigerator but changed its delivery routine. By comparing time records with actual work, the students avoided replacing equipment that was working correctly and helped reduce food loss. The students also compared how long the door remained open on ordinary days. It was usually less than two minutes, but large-delivery days averaged nearly nine minutes. They placed a rolling cart beside the sorting table so chilled items could be grouped together before the door opened. Volunteers then recorded both temperature and door-open time for another ten days. Short door openings matched the more stable temperatures. The pantry added the new routine to its volunteer guide and kept the log in case the pattern changed later.
passages.fullTranslation: 地域の食品配布所では、牛乳や調理済み食品を二台の冷蔵庫に保管していました。ボランティアは、冷蔵庫Bの温度記録が目標範囲を短時間上回ることがあり、消費期限前でも食品を捨てる場合があることに気づきました。すぐ冷蔵庫を交換しようという人もいました。生徒グループは一か月分の温度記録と配送時刻を一緒に調べました。温度上昇の多くは午後4時から4時30分に起き、その時間には複数の箱が届き、ボランティアが食品を仕分ける間、扉が開いたままになっていました。大きな配送がない日は温度が安定していました。生徒たちは、まずテーブル上で箱を仕分け、入れる準備ができた食品だけをまとめて冷蔵庫へ入れる方法を試しました。次の一週間の記録では温度上昇が小さく、時間も短くなりました。技術者も冷蔵庫を確認し、機械の故障はないと判断しました。配布所は冷蔵庫を使い続け、配送時の作業方法を変えました。時刻記録と実際の作業を比べたことで、正常な機器を交換せず、食品廃棄も減らせました。 生徒たちは通常の日に扉が開いている時間も比べました。普段は2分未満でしたが、大きな配送の日は平均約9分でした。そこで仕分け台の横に移動式ワゴンを置き、冷蔵品をまとめてから扉を開けられるようにしました。さらに10日間、温度と開扉時間の両方を記録すると、扉を短く開けた日は温度もより安定していました。配布所は新しい手順をボランティア用案内に加え、今後傾向が変わった場合に確認できるよう記録も続けました。

sentences: A community pantry stored milk and prepared food
in two refrigerators.
Volunteers noticed
that food from Refrigerator B was sometimes thrown away before its use-by date
because the temperature record showed short rises above the target range.
Some people wanted to replace the refrigerator immediately.
A group of students examined one month of temperature logs
together with delivery times.
Most rises happened between 4:00 and 4:30 p.m.,
when several boxes were delivered
and the door stayed open while volunteers sorted food.
On days without a large delivery,
the temperature remained stable.
The students tested a new process:
boxes were sorted on a table first,
and the refrigerator door was opened only when items were ready to be placed inside.
The next week's log showed smaller and shorter temperature rises.
A technician still checked the refrigerator
and found no mechanical problem.
The pantry kept the refrigerator
but changed its delivery routine.
By comparing time records with actual work,
the students avoided replacing equipment that was working correctly
and helped reduce food loss.
The students also compared
how long the door remained open on ordinary days.
It was usually less than two minutes,
but large-delivery days averaged nearly nine minutes.
They placed a rolling cart beside the sorting table
so chilled items could be grouped together before the door opened.
Volunteers then recorded both temperature and door-open time
for another ten days.
Short door openings matched the more stable temperatures.
The pantry added the new routine to its volunteer guide
and kept the log
in case the pattern changed later.

questions.reason: The pronoun refers to the immediately preceding measure: door-open time on ordinary days.

questionSetB.evidenceJp: 普段は2分未満でしたが、大きな配送の日は平均約9分でした。
questionSetB.reason: The passage gives both times directly for comparison.

questionSetB.prompt: What happened after the students tested the new process?
questionSetB.answer: The next week's temperature rises were smaller and shorter.
questionSetB.evidence: The next week's log showed smaller and shorter temperature rises.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 次の一週間の記録では温度上昇が小さく、時間も短くなりました。
questionSetB.reason: This is the direct result reported after changing the delivery process.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the students place a rolling cart beside the sorting table?
questionSetB.answer: So chilled items could be grouped together before the refrigerator door was opened.
questionSetB.evidence: They placed a rolling cart beside the sorting table so chilled items could be grouped together before the door opened.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: そこで仕分け台の横に移動式ワゴンを置き、冷蔵品をまとめてから扉を開けられるようにしました。
questionSetB.reason: Grouping chilled items first helped shorten each door opening.

questionSetB.reason: The log remained useful for future monitoring even after the immediate problem improved.

passages.title: The Safety Notice with an Extra Word
passages.body: Students preparing a bilingual safety guide compared the Japanese and English notices for a school workshop. One English sentence said that “all visitors” must wear protective glasses near the cutting machine. The Japanese original, however, required glasses only for visitors who entered the marked work area. The word “all” had been added during an earlier rewrite. It made the English rule stricter than the original and could confuse people waiting outside the work area. The students checked the teacher's official rule and changed the English notice to match it. They also asked another student to read both versions independently. The final pair gave the same condition in both languages. The group learned that adding a familiar word can still change the meaning of a safety message. To prevent the same problem later, the team marked conditions such as “in the work area” in a separate review column. Translators had to check that column before approving a sentence. The teacher preferred this method because it protected the exact rule without forcing both languages to use identical word order.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校の作業室用に二言語の安全案内を準備していた生徒たちは、日本語と英語の掲示を比べました。英語の一文には、切断機の近くでは「すべての来訪者」が保護メガネを着けなければならないとありました。しかし日本語の原文では、印の付いた作業区域へ入る来訪者だけが対象でした。「all」という語が以前の書き直しで加わり、英語の規則が原文より厳しくなっていました。そのため作業区域の外で待つ人まで混乱する可能性がありました。生徒たちは先生の正式な規則を確認し、英語掲示を原文と同じ条件に直しました。さらに別の生徒に二つの版をそれぞれ読んでもらいました。最終版では両言語が同じ条件を示しました。よく知っている一語を足すだけでも、安全案内の意味が変わることを学びました。 同じ問題を防ぐため、チームは「作業区域内」のような条件を別の確認欄に記録することにしました。翻訳担当者は文を承認する前にその欄も確認します。先生は、両言語の語順を同じにしなくても規則の正確な条件を守れるとして、この方法を評価しました。
