passages.title: The Harbor Walk Event Route
passages.body: A town planned a Saturday walking event from Harbor Station to the old lighthouse. The usual seaside path was easy to follow, but part of it would be closed from 10:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. for repair work. Organizers had to choose a route for three groups leaving the station at 9:40, 10:20, and 11:00. A tide table also showed that the lower beach path could not be used safely after 10:45 because the tide would cover a narrow section. A shuttle bus left the market square for the lighthouse at 10:50 and 11:50. The first group could use the seaside path and reach the lighthouse before the closure. The second group would reach the repair area after the closure, and the beach path would become unsafe before the group finished it. Organizers therefore directed that group to the market square and the 10:50 shuttle. The third group used the inland road to the market square and took the 11:50 shuttle. The route board explained why different groups received different directions. The safest plan did not depend on distance alone; departure time, construction, tide, and bus service all had to be considered together. The organizers tested the plan by estimating walking times. The seaside route normally took forty minutes, the inland walk to the market square took twenty-five minutes, and the lower beach path needed about thirty-five minutes. This confirmed that the 10:20 group could not simply hurry through the closed section. They also considered asking that group to wait until 1:00, but that would delay lunch and separate them from the event program. The shuttle solution kept their arrival close to the other groups. On the route board, a blue line showed the normal seaside route, a green line showed the inland route, and a red mark identified the closed section. Next to the tide table, organizers added a note explaining that “open now” did not mean “safe for the whole walk.” Volunteers at Harbor Station received the same information so they could answer questions consistently. On the event morning, each group leader checked the current board before departure because weather or repair work could still change the plan.
passages.fullTranslation: 町は土曜日に港駅から古い灯台まで歩く行事を計画しました。普段の海沿いの道は分かりやすいのですが、その一部が修理のため午前10時30分から午後1時まで通行止めになります。主催者は、9時40分、10時20分、11時に駅を出る三つのグループの道を決める必要がありました。潮位表には、干潮時に使える下側の浜辺の道も、10時45分以降は狭い部分が潮で覆われ安全に使えないとありました。市場広場から灯台へは10時50分と11時50分にシャトルバスが出ます。最初のグループは海沿いの道を使い、通行止めが始まる前に灯台へ着けます。二番目のグループは修理区間に着くのが遅くなり、浜辺の道も歩き終える前に危険になります。そのため主催者は市場広場へ向かわせ、10時50分のシャトルを使わせました。三番目のグループは内陸の道で市場広場へ行き、11時50分のシャトルを利用しました。案内板には、グループごとに違う道を使う理由も示しました。安全な計画は距離だけでは決められず、出発時刻、工事、潮、バスを合わせて考える必要がありました。 主催者は歩行時間を見積もって計画を確かめました。海沿いの通常ルートは約40分、市場広場までの内陸ルートは25分、下側の浜辺の道は約35分かかります。このため10時20分のグループが急いで通行止め区間を抜ける案は使えないと確認できました。1時まで待つ案も考えましたが、それでは昼食が遅れ、行事の予定から外れてしまいます。シャトルを使えば他のグループに近い時刻に到着できます。案内板では通常の海沿いルートを青、内陸ルートを緑、通行止め区間を赤で示しました。潮位表の横には、「今通れる」ことと「歩き終えるまで安全」なことは同じではないという説明も加えました。港駅のボランティアにも同じ情報を渡し、質問への答えが人によって変わらないようにしました。当日の朝も、天候や工事状況が変わる可能性があるため、各班のリーダーが出発前に最新の案内板を確認しました。

passages.title: The Interview Answer Cut in Half
passages.body: A school newspaper interviewed a local baker about reducing plastic bags. In a draft article, the baker was quoted as saying, “Customers do not want paper bags.” The statement sounded clear, but one student remembered a longer answer. The team listened to the original recording. The baker had actually said, “Some customers do not want paper bags on rainy days because they worry about water, but most accept them when we explain the new covers.” The first draft had kept only the beginning and changed the impression of the interview. The students replaced the short quote with a summary that included both the concern and the condition under which customers accepted paper bags. They also saved the recording time beside their notes. The correction made the article less dramatic but more accurate. The editor then asked each writer to label notes as direct quote, summary, or background fact. That small change made it easier to see when shortened wording needed to be checked against the recording before publication.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校新聞は、プラスチック袋を減らす取り組みについて地域のパン店へインタビューしました。記事の下書きには、店主の言葉として「お客さんは紙袋を望んでいません」と引用されていました。はっきりした発言に見えましたが、一人の生徒はもっと長い答えだったと覚えていました。チームが元の録音を聞くと、実際には「雨の日はぬれることを心配して紙袋を望まないお客さんもいますが、新しいカバーについて説明すると、多くの人は受け入れてくれます」と話していました。最初の下書きは前半だけを残し、インタビューの印象を変えていました。生徒たちは短い引用をやめ、心配の内容と紙袋を受け入れる条件の両方を含む要約に直しました。またメモの横に録音時刻も残しました。修正後の記事は派手さは減りましたが、より正確になりました。 編集担当はさらに、メモを「直接引用」「要約」「背景事実」に分けて表示するよう決めました。この小さな変更で、短くした表現を公開前に録音と照合すべき場所が分かりやすくなりました。

passages.title: Two Surveys of the Same Park
passages.body: Two student groups surveyed use of Sakura Park and reached different conclusions. Group A visited on a sunny Saturday afternoon and counted many families near the playground. Group B visited on a cloudy Tuesday morning and found mostly older adults walking near the pond. At first, each group believed the other had counted incorrectly. They compared their survey sheets and discovered that both groups had followed the same counting method. The difference came from when and where they had observed the park. To obtain a broader picture, the students returned four times: weekday morning, weekday afternoon, weekend morning, and weekend afternoon. They counted users in the playground, pond path, and open field separately. The combined results showed that the park served different groups at different times. Families were common near the playground on weekends, while walkers used the pond path more steadily through the week. Instead of choosing one survey as correct, the students explained the conditions behind both. Their final report recommended collecting data across several time periods before changing park facilities. The students also compared weather within the new survey. Weekend afternoon use dropped during light rain, while the pond path still had several regular walkers. This helped them avoid treating every difference as a weekday-versus-weekend effect. They included the weather beside each count in the final table and wrote that future surveys should use the same categories. A park manager said the richer record was more useful. It showed how many people came and which spaces they used under different conditions.
passages.fullTranslation: 二つの生徒グループがさくら公園の利用状況を調べましたが、異なる結論になりました。A班は晴れた土曜日の午後に訪れ、遊具の近くに多くの家族を数えました。B班は曇った火曜日の朝に訪れ、池の周りを歩く高齢者が中心でした。最初は互いに数え方が間違っていると思いました。しかし調査用紙を比べると、どちらも同じ方法で人数を数えていました。違いは、観察した時間と場所から生まれていました。より広い様子を知るため、生徒たちは平日朝・平日午後・休日朝・休日午後の四回、公園へ戻りました。そして遊具、池の道、広場を分けて人数を記録しました。まとめた結果から、公園は時間によって異なる人々に使われていると分かりました。休日には遊具近くに家族が多く、池の道は一週間を通して歩く人が比較的安定していました。一方の調査だけを正しいとせず、両方の結果が生まれた条件を説明しました。最終報告では、公園設備を変える前に複数の時間帯でデータを集めることを勧めました。 生徒たちは新しい調査の中で天候による違いも比べました。休日の午後でも弱い雨の日は利用者が減りましたが、池の道にはいつものように歩く人が何人かいました。この結果から、すべての差を平日と休日だけの違いとは考えないようにしました。最終表では各人数の横に天候も記し、今後の調査でも同じ分類を使うべきだと書きました。公園管理者は、人数だけでなく異なる条件でどの場所が使われたか分かるため、この詳しい記録の方が役立つと話しました。

sentences: Two student groups surveyed use of Sakura Park
and reached different conclusions.
Group A visited on a sunny Saturday afternoon
and counted many families near the playground.
Group B visited on a cloudy Tuesday morning
and found mostly older adults walking near the pond.
At first,
each group believed the other had counted incorrectly.
They compared their survey sheets
and discovered that both groups had followed the same counting method.
The difference came from
when and where they had observed the park.
To obtain a broader picture,
the students returned four times: weekday morning, weekday afternoon, weekend morning, and weekend afternoon.
They counted users in the playground, pond path, and open field separately.
The combined results showed
that the park served different groups at different times.
Families were common near the playground on weekends,
while walkers used the pond path more steadily through the week.
Instead of choosing one survey as correct,
the students explained the conditions behind both.
Their final report recommended collecting data across several time periods
before changing park facilities.
The students also compared weather
within the new survey.
Weekend afternoon use dropped during light rain,
while the pond path still had several regular walkers.
This helped them avoid treating every difference
as a weekday-versus-weekend effect.
They included the weather beside each count
in the final table
and wrote that future surveys should use the same categories.
A park manager said
the richer record was more useful.
It showed how many people came
and which spaces they used under different conditions.

questions.prompt: Why did the two student groups originally reach different conclusions about Sakura Park?
questions.answer: They observed the park at different times, in different weather, and in different areas.
questions.evidence: The difference came from when and where they had observed the park.
questions.evidenceJp: 違いは、観察した時間と場所から生まれていました。
questions.reason: Both groups used the same counting method, so the observation conditions explained the different results.

questions.prompt: What did Group A see during its first survey?
questions.answer: Many families near the playground on a sunny Saturday afternoon.
questions.evidence: Group A visited on a sunny Saturday afternoon and counted many families near the playground.
questions.evidenceJp: A班は晴れた土曜日の午後に訪れ、遊具の近くに多くの家族を数えました。
questions.reason: The passage directly states Group A's time, weather, location, and main users.

questions.prompt: How did the students broaden the second round of observation?
questions.answer: They surveyed four time periods and counted the playground, pond path, and open field separately.
questions.evidence: To obtain a broader picture, the students returned four times: weekday morning, weekday afternoon, weekend morning, and weekend afternoon. They counted users in the playground, pond path, and open field separately.
questions.evidenceJp: より広い様子を知るため、生徒たちは平日朝・平日午後・休日朝・休日午後の四回、公園へ戻りました。そして遊具、池の道、広場を分けて人数を記録しました。
questions.reason: The new design expanded both time coverage and spatial coverage.

questions.prompt: What did the combined results show about the park?
questions.answer: Different groups used different parts of the park at different times, so no single short survey represented all park use.
questions.evidence: The combined results showed that the park served different groups at different times.
questions.evidenceJp: まとめた結果から、公園は時間によって異なる人々に使われていると分かりました。
questions.reason: The broader survey revealed patterns that neither original one-time observation could show alone.

questions.prompt: Why did the students avoid choosing one of the first surveys as the correct one?
questions.answer: Because both groups had counted correctly under different observation conditions.
questions.evidence: Instead of choosing one survey as correct, the students explained the conditions behind both.
questions.evidenceJp: 一方の調査だけを正しいとせず、両方の結果が生まれた条件を説明しました。
questions.reason: The conflict came from sampling conditions, not from one group's counting error.

questionSetB.prompt: What pattern did the combined survey find near the playground?
questionSetB.answer: Families were common there on weekends.
questionSetB.evidence: Families were common near the playground on weekends, while walkers used the pond path more steadily through the week.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 休日には遊具近くに家族が多く、池の道は一週間を通して歩く人が比較的安定していました。
questionSetB.reason: This was one of the location-and-time patterns found after the broader survey.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the students record the weather beside each count?
questionSetB.answer: So they would not mistake weather effects for simple weekday-versus-weekend differences.
questionSetB.evidence: This helped them avoid treating every difference as a weekday-versus-weekend effect. They included the weather beside each count in the final table.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: この結果から、すべての差を平日と休日だけの違いとは考えないようにしました。最終表では各人数の横に天候も記し、
questionSetB.reason: Light rain changed weekend afternoon use, showing that day type alone could not explain every difference.

questionSetB.prompt: What happened during light rain on a weekend afternoon?
questionSetB.answer: Overall park use dropped, but several regular walkers still used the pond path.
questionSetB.evidence: Weekend afternoon use dropped during light rain, while the pond path still had several regular walkers.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 休日の午後でも弱い雨の日は利用者が減りましたが、池の道にはいつものように歩く人が何人かいました。
questionSetB.reason: The passage contrasts the drop in general use with continued use of the pond path.

questionSetB.prompt: Complete the recommendation: Before changing park facilities, collect data across several ____ and keep observation categories consistent.
questionSetB.answer: time periods
questionSetB.evidence: Their final report recommended collecting data across several time periods before changing park facilities.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 最終報告では、公園設備を変える前に複数の時間帯でデータを集めることを勧めました。
questionSetB.reason: The original disagreement arose because the first surveys each covered only one limited time and condition.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the park manager find the richer record more useful?
questionSetB.answer: It showed both how many people came and which spaces they used under different conditions.
questionSetB.evidence: A park manager said the richer record was more useful. It showed how many people came and which spaces they used under different conditions.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 公園管理者は、人数だけでなく異なる条件でどの場所が使われたか分かるため、この詳しい記録の方が役立つと話しました。
questionSetB.reason: The expanded data gave information about both quantity and patterns of space use, which is more useful for facility decisions.

passages.title: The Science Center Group Plan
passages.body: A class of fifty-four students planned a visit to a science center. They would arrive at 10:00 and leave at 12:30. The center offered a robotics workshop at 10:20 and 11:20. The workshop room held eighteen students. A planetarium show began at 10:30 and 11:30, and its room held thirty-six. The class was divided into three groups of eighteen. Group A could attend robotics at 10:20 while Groups B and C watched the 10:30 planetarium show together. At 11:20, Group B could attend robotics. Group A would use the exhibition floor, and Group C would remain there until the 11:30 planetarium show was no longer useful for the whole group because only thirty minutes would remain before departure. The students changed the plan: Group C attended robotics at 11:20 instead of Group B, while Group B used the exhibition floor. Group C had already seen the 10:30 planetarium show with Group B, so this created a conflict. They checked the schedule again and realized only two robotics sessions were available, so not all three groups could take robotics. The final plan gave robotics to Groups A and B and the planetarium to all students in two rotations, while Group C used an interactive lab instead of robotics. The class chose a plan that respected capacities and accepted that every group could not do every activity. The class then built a timetable for every twenty-minute block. From 10:00 to 10:20, all groups received orientation. Group A entered robotics at 10:20, while Groups B and C went to the 10:30 planetarium. After that show, Group B reached the 11:20 robotics workshop in time. Group C moved to the interactive lab, where eighteen students fit comfortably. Group A used the exhibition floor after robotics. At 11:30, Group A joined other visitors in the planetarium because enough seats remained, while Groups B and C continued activities they had not yet completed. The teacher checked walking time between rooms and required a ten-minute movement margin, so no group was scheduled in two distant places back-to-back. The final chart used three colors, one for each group, and showed meeting points as well as activity times. Students accepted that Group C would not do robotics because trying to force all three groups into two workshops would violate the room capacity. Instead, the interactive lab gave that group a hands-on activity of similar length. Everyone returned to the entrance by 12:20, leaving ten minutes for attendance before departure.
passages.fullTranslation: 54人のクラスが科学館見学を計画しました。10時に到着し、12時30分に出発します。科学館ではロボット教室が10時20分と11時20分にあり、教室の定員は18人です。プラネタリウムは10時30分と11時30分に始まり、定員は36人です。クラスは18人ずつ三班に分かれました。A班が10時20分のロボット教室へ行き、その間B班とC班の36人が10時30分のプラネタリウムを見ることはできます。11時20分にはB班がロボット教室へ行けます。A班は展示フロアを利用し、C班も展示を続ける案を考えましたが、11時30分のプラネタリウムを全員のために使うには出発まで30分しか残りません。生徒たちは別案も検討しましたが、日程を再確認するとロボット教室は二回しかなく、三班すべてが参加することはできないと分かりました。最終的にA班とB班がロボット教室を利用し、プラネタリウムは二回に分けて全員が見るようにし、C班はロボットの代わりに体験実験室を使う計画にしました。定員と時刻を守り、全班がすべての活動をできるわけではないことを受け入れた計画です。 クラスは次に20分ごとの詳しい予定表を作りました。10時から10時20分までは全班が説明を受けます。A班は10時20分のロボット教室へ入り、B班とC班は10時30分のプラネタリウムへ行きます。上映後、B班には11時20分のロボット教室へ移動する時間があります。C班は18人が十分入れる体験実験室へ移動します。A班はロボット教室の後に展示フロアを利用します。11時30分には空席があるプラネタリウムへA班が入り、B班とC班はまだ行っていない活動を続けます。先生は部屋間の移動時間も確認し、10分の移動余裕を必ず取るようにしたため、離れた場所を連続して予定する班はありません。最終表では三班を別々の色で示し、活動時刻だけでなく集合場所も書きました。二回しかないロボット教室へ三班すべてを無理に入れると定員違反になるため、C班が参加しないことを受け入れました。その代わり、同程度の時間の体験実験を行います。全員が12時20分までに入口へ戻り、出発前に10分間出席確認できる計画になりました。

passages.title: The Crop in the Corner of the Photo
passages.body: A student reporter took a photo of a crowded recycling event and cropped it for the school website. The cropped image showed several bags on the ground and made the area look disorganized. Before publishing, another student opened the original photo. In the corner, volunteers were sorting the bags into labeled groups, but that part had disappeared from the crop. The team realized that the smaller image could give readers the wrong idea about what was happening. They selected a wider crop that included both the waiting bags and the sorting table. The caption was also changed from “Bags pile up at the event” to “Volunteers sort a busy group of donations.” The new version still showed the crowd but also showed the work that explained it. Before choosing the new crop, the students showed both versions to six classmates without revealing the intended caption. Several described the narrow image as “unmanaged,” while the wider image led them to mention sorting work. That response supported the change.
passages.fullTranslation: 生徒記者が混雑したリサイクル行事を撮影し、学校ウェブサイト用に写真を切り取りました。切り取った写真には地面に置かれた袋がいくつも写り、会場が整理されていないように見えました。公開前に別の生徒が元の写真を開きました。写真の隅ではボランティアが袋を表示ごとに仕分けていましたが、その部分が切り取りで消えていました。小さくした写真だけでは、何が起きているかについて読者に間違った印象を与える可能性があると気づきました。そこで待っている袋と仕分け台の両方が入る広い切り取りに変えました。説明文も「行事で袋が積み上がる」から「ボランティアが多くの寄付品を仕分ける」へ変更しました。新しい写真も混雑は示しますが、その理由となる作業も同時に見せています。 新しい切り取りを決める前に、意図した説明文を見せず二つの写真を6人のクラスメートに見てもらいました。狭い写真では「管理されていない」と表現する人が何人もいましたが、広い写真では仕分け作業について話す人が増えました。この反応も変更を裏づけました。

passages.title: Keep, Repair, or Move the Bike Racks?
passages.body: Students studied three bicycle racks near a community center. Rack A was used by twenty-five people a day and had light rust on two bars. Rack B was used by only eight people, but users said it was convenient because it stood beside the main entrance. Rack C was almost new, yet it was used by just three people because rainwater collected around it after storms. A maintenance company estimated that repairing Rack A would cost much less than replacing it. Moving Rack C to higher ground would cost more than a small repair but less than buying a new rack. The students recommended repairing Rack A, keeping Rack B as it was, and moving Rack C. They did not rank the racks only by age or appearance. sentences: Students studied three bicycle racks
near a community center.
Rack A was used by twenty-five people a day
and had light rust on two bars.
Rack B was used by only eight people,
but users said it was convenient
because it stood beside the main entrance.
Rack C was almost new,
yet it was used by just three people
because rainwater collected around it after storms.
A maintenance company estimated
that repairing Rack A would cost much less than replacing it.
Moving Rack C to higher ground would cost more than a small repair
but less than buying a new rack.
The students recommended repairing Rack A,
keeping Rack B as it was,
and moving Rack C.
They did not rank the racks only by age or appearance.
Use, location, cost, and the cause of each problem
led to different choices.
Six months later,
Rack C was used more often in its drier location,
while Rack A remained safe after repair.
The mixed plan used the budget
where it solved an actual problem.
The students also counted empty spaces at different times
instead of relying on one daily average.
Rack B filled briefly during evening meetings,
which explained why users valued its position
despite the lower average.
For Rack C,
they observed where riders parked when puddles formed
and found several bicycles attached to a fence on higher ground.
After moving Rack C,
those bicycles shifted to the rack.
The follow-up supported the idea
that poor use had reflected the wet location
rather than a lack of demand.

passages.title: The Rain-Safe Market Schedule
passages.body: A community market planned outdoor activities from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. The weather forecast showed light rain before 10:00, a dry period from 10:00 to noon, and heavier rain after 12:30. The site map had two covered areas: a small tent for thirty people and a large hall for eighty. A children's craft activity needed forty seats and was scheduled for 9:30. A music performance expected seventy visitors at 11:00, and a local food talk for twenty-five people was planned at 1:00. Organizers could not simply move every event indoors because the hall was being used for market tables until 10:30. They moved the craft activity to 10:15 in the hall after some tables were cleared. The 11:00 music performance stayed outdoors during the dry period, with the hall ready as a backup. The 1:00 food talk moved to the small tent because its expected audience fit the space and heavier rain was likely. The final notice explained the changes and asked visitors to check the board at 10:45 for the music decision. By matching weather, capacity, and room availability, the organizers created a schedule that could change safely without cancelling the whole market. The team also prepared decision rules instead of relying on a last-minute guess. If rain at 10:45 was only light and radar showed the dry period continuing, the music performance would stay outside. If heavier rain arrived early, staff would move chairs into the hall and delay the start by ten minutes. A volunteer counted available hall seats after the market tables were reduced, confirming that seventy visitors could enter without blocking exits. For the craft activity, families registered at the information desk so organizers knew whether the forty-seat estimate remained reasonable. The small tent was reserved for the food talk from 12:40, leaving twenty minutes for setup before the speaker began. Signs at the entrance used the same activity names and times as the printed program, reducing confusion when a location changed. After the market, organizers compared attendance with the revised schedule and found that no activity had to be cancelled. They saved the weather-and-capacity table as a model for future outdoor events, while noting that new forecasts must always replace the old numbers.
passages.fullTranslation: 地域市場では午前9時から午後2時まで屋外活動を計画していました。天気予報は10時前に弱い雨、10時から正午までは雨がやみ、12時30分以降は強めの雨を示していました。会場には屋根のある場所が二つあり、小さなテントは30人、大きなホールは80人入れます。子ども向け工作は40席必要で9時30分開始、音楽演奏は70人ほどを見込み11時、地域の食についての話は25人で午後1時の予定でした。ホールは10時30分まで市場の売り場に使われるため、すべてを単純に室内へ移すことはできません。工作は一部の売り場を片づけた後の10時15分にホールで行うことにしました。11時の音楽演奏は雨のない時間に屋外で予定どおり行い、必要ならホールへ移れるよう準備しました。午後1時の話は、人数が入る小テントへ移しました。その時間は強い雨の可能性が高いからです。最終案内には変更点を示し、音楽については10時45分の掲示で最終確認するよう伝えました。天気、定員、場所が使える時刻を合わせることで、市場全体を中止せず安全に変更できる計画になりました。 チームは直前の勘だけに頼らず、判断ルールも準備しました。10時45分の雨が弱く、雨雲情報でも雨のない時間が続くなら音楽演奏は屋外で行います。強い雨が早く来れば、係がホールへいすを移し、開始を10分遅らせます。市場の机を減らした後のホールの利用可能席も数え、70人が非常口をふさがず入れることを確認しました。工作については案内所で家族の参加を受け付け、40席という見込みが妥当か確認できるようにしました。小テントは12時40分から食の話のために確保し、講師開始前に20分の準備時間を取りました。入口の案内は印刷プログラムと同じ活動名と時刻を使い、場所が変わっても混乱しにくくしました。行事後に参加者数と変更後の予定を比べると、中止になった活動はありませんでした。主催者は天気と定員を組み合わせた表を次回の屋外行事の参考として保存しましたが、予報数値は毎回最新情報へ置き換える必要があることも記しました。

sentences: A community market planned outdoor activities
from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.
The weather forecast showed light rain before 10:00,
a dry period from 10:00 to noon,
and heavier rain after 12:30.
The site map had two covered areas:
a small tent for thirty people
and a large hall for eighty.
A children's craft activity needed forty seats
and was scheduled for 9:30.
A music performance expected seventy visitors at 11:00,
and a local food talk for twenty-five people was planned at 1:00.
Organizers could not simply move every event indoors
because the hall was being used for market tables until 10:30.
They moved the craft activity to 10:15 in the hall
after some tables were cleared.
The 11:00 music performance stayed outdoors
during the dry period,
with the hall ready as a backup.
The 1:00 food talk moved to the small tent
because its expected audience fit the space
and heavier rain was likely.
The final notice explained the changes
and asked visitors to check the board at 10:45
for the music decision.
By matching weather, capacity, and room availability,
the organizers created a schedule
that could change safely without cancelling the whole market.
The team also prepared decision rules
instead of relying on a last-minute guess.
If rain at 10:45 was only light
and radar showed the dry period continuing,
the music performance would stay outside.
If heavier rain arrived early,
staff would move chairs into the hall
and delay the start by ten minutes.
A volunteer counted available hall seats
after the market tables were reduced,
confirming that seventy visitors could enter without blocking exits.
For the craft activity,
families registered at the information desk
so organizers knew whether the forty-seat estimate remained reasonable.
The small tent was reserved for the food talk from 12:40,
leaving twenty minutes for setup
before the speaker began.
Signs at the entrance used the same activity names and times
as the printed program,
reducing confusion when a location changed.
After the market,
organizers compared attendance with the revised schedule
and found that no activity had to be cancelled.
They saved the weather-and-capacity table
as a model for future outdoor events,
while noting that new forecasts must always replace the old numbers.

questions.prompt: What was the main challenge in making the market schedule?
questions.answer: The organizers had to match changing weather with event sizes and the times when covered spaces were available.
questions.evidence: By matching weather, capacity, and room availability, the organizers created a schedule that could change safely without cancelling the whole market.
questions.evidenceJp: 天気、定員、場所が使える時刻を合わせることで、市場全体を中止せず安全に変更できる計画になりました。
questions.reason: The passage centers on balancing weather, capacity, and room availability rather than moving every event indoors.

questions.prompt: Why was the craft activity moved to 10:15 in the hall?
questions.answer: Because the craft needed forty seats, and the hall became usable after some market tables were cleared.
questions.evidence: They moved the craft activity to 10:15 in the hall after some tables were cleared.
questions.evidenceJp: 工作は一部の売り場を片づけた後の10時15分にホールで行うことにしました。
questions.reason: The smaller tent could not hold forty people, while the hall could be used once part of the market setup was cleared.

questions.prompt: Why was the 1:00 food talk moved to the small tent?
questions.answer: Its expected audience fit the tent, and heavier rain was likely by that time.
questions.evidence: The 1:00 food talk moved to the small tent because its expected audience fit the space and heavier rain was likely.
questions.evidenceJp: 午後1時の話は、人数が入る小テントへ移しました。その時間は強い雨の可能性が高いからです。
questions.reason: The decision matched both the audience size and the weather forecast.

questions.prompt: What were visitors told to check at 10:45?
questions.answer: They were told to check the board for the final decision about the music performance.
questions.evidence: The final notice explained the changes and asked visitors to check the board at 10:45 for the music decision.
questions.evidenceJp: 最終案内には変更点を示し、音楽については10時45分の掲示で最終確認するよう伝えました。
questions.reason: The music location depended on the weather at that time, so the board carried the final decision.

questions.prompt: Why was the hall a practical backup for the 11:00 music performance?
questions.answer: By then the hall could hold the expected seventy visitors and was no longer fully occupied by market tables.
questions.evidence: A volunteer counted available hall seats after the market tables were reduced, confirming that seventy visitors could enter without blocking exits.
questions.evidenceJp: 市場の机を減らした後のホールの利用可能席も数え、70人が非常口をふさがず入れることを確認しました。
questions.reason: The backup was only practical because the hall had enough safe space after the market-table area was reduced.

passages.title: The Percentage without Its Question
passages.body: A poster in the school hall said, “Seventy percent of students prefer digital books.” The number was repeated in a club presentation, but Aya wanted to see the original survey. She found that the actual question had been, “When carrying three or more textbooks, would you prefer a digital version for at least one book?” Seventy percent had answered yes. The survey did not ask whether students preferred digital books in general. The club changed its presentation to say that many students wanted a digital option when carrying several textbooks. The percentage remained the same, but the claim became narrower and matched the question that produced the number. Aya learned that a number cannot be understood fully without knowing what was asked. The club added the original survey question below the graph so readers could judge the number themselves. They also stopped using the word “prefer” by itself when a choice depended on a particular situation.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校の廊下のポスターには「生徒の70パーセントが電子書籍を好む」と書かれていました。その数字は部活動の発表でも使われましたが、アヤは元のアンケートを確認したいと思いました。実際の質問は「教科書を3冊以上持ち運ぶとき、少なくとも1冊を電子版にしたいですか」でした。70パーセントが「はい」と答えていました。この調査は、普段から電子書籍の方が好きかどうかを尋ねたものではありません。部は発表を「複数の教科書を運ぶとき、電子版の選択肢を望む生徒が多い」と直しました。数字は同じでも、主張を狭くして、数字を生んだ質問と一致させました。数字を十分理解するには、何を尋ねたのかを知る必要があるとアヤは学びました。 部はグラフの下に元の質問文も載せ、読者自身が数字の意味を判断できるようにしました。また、特定の状況での選択を示すときは「好む」という言葉だけで一般化しないことにしました。

passages.title: The Community Garden Shade Record
passages.body: A community garden had two vegetable beds that produced very different amounts of tomatoes. Bed A produced almost twice as many as Bed B, and some volunteers wanted to replace the soil in Bed B. Students examined the garden records before agreeing. The soil tests from both beds were similar, but the sunlight records were not. A new building cast shade over Bed B for part of the afternoon, while Bed A received direct sun for several more hours. The students also checked growth notes from leafy vegetables. Those plants had grown well in Bed B even after the building was completed. The group proposed planting more tomatoes in Bed A and using Bed B for vegetables that could grow with less direct sun. They also planned one small tomato test in Bed B rather than removing tomatoes completely. The next season, total harvest from the two beds increased. The students did not treat lower tomato production as proof of poor soil. By comparing several records, they found that the two beds had different strengths and adjusted planting to match them. To test the new plan fairly, volunteers recorded planting dates, watering, and harvest weights for both beds. They used the same tomato variety in the small Bed B test, so a different variety would not confuse the comparison. The test tomatoes in Bed B produced less fruit but remained healthy, while leafy vegetables used the shaded space effectively. These results supported keeping a small experiment while using most of each bed for crops suited to its light conditions.
passages.fullTranslation: 地域の菜園には二つの野菜区画があり、トマトの収穫量が大きく違っていました。A区画はBのほぼ二倍収穫できたため、Bの土を入れ替えようというボランティアもいました。生徒たちは賛成する前に記録を調べました。二つの区画の土壌検査は似ていましたが、日当たりの記録は違いました。新しい建物の影でBは午後の一部が日陰になり、Aは数時間長く直射日光を受けていました。生徒は葉物野菜の成長記録も確認しました。葉物は建物完成後もBでよく育っていました。そこでAにはトマトを増やし、Bには直射日光が少なくても育つ野菜を多く植える案を出しました。ただしBからトマトを完全になくさず、小さな試験区画を残しました。次の季節には二つの区画全体の収穫量が増えました。トマトの収穫が少ないことを、すぐ土が悪い証拠とは考えませんでした。複数の記録を比べ、それぞれの区画の強みに合う植え方へ変えたのです。 新しい計画を公平に確かめるため、ボランティアは両区画の植え付け日、水やり、収穫重量を記録しました。Bの小さな試験区画でも同じ品種のトマトを使い、品種差が比較を乱さないようにしました。Bの試験トマトは実の数は少ないものの健康に育ち、葉物野菜は日陰の場所を有効に使えました。この結果から、小さな実験は残しつつ、各区画の大部分を日当たり条件に合う作物へ使う方針が支持されました。

passages.title: Three Accounts of the Lost Bag
passages.body: A bag disappeared from a bench during a school event. Three students gave different accounts. Student A said she saw the bag on the bench at 1:10. Student B said a tall person carried a dark bag away at about 1:20. Student C said the owner returned at 1:25 and looked surprised. Some committee members immediately decided that the tall person had taken the missing bag. Others pointed out that Student B had not seen the bench and could not identify the bag. The committee separated direct observations from guesses. They checked a photo taken at 1:18 and saw the missing bag still on the bench. Later, the owner found it at the information desk, where a staff member had moved it for safety. The careful timeline prevented an unsupported accusation. The committee wrote the confirmed times in one column and uncertain descriptions in another. This made it clear that height and bag color were useful leads but not proof of identity. Staff members later adopted the same format for other lost-property reports.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校行事中、ベンチからかばんがなくなりました。三人の生徒が異なる話をしました。Aは1時10分にベンチの上にかばんを見たと言いました。Bは1時20分ごろ背の高い人が暗い色のかばんを持って去るのを見たと言いました。Cは1時25分に持ち主が戻り、驚いていたと言いました。委員の一部はすぐ、背の高い人がなくなったかばんを持っていったと判断しました。しかしBはベンチそのものを見ておらず、そのかばんが同じ物だと確認できていないという意見も出ました。委員会は直接見たことと推測を分けました。1時18分に撮られた写真を確認すると、なくなったかばんはまだベンチにありました。後で持ち主は案内所でかばんを見つけました。安全のため職員が移していたのです。時系列を丁寧に確認したことで、根拠のない非難を避けられました。 委員会は確認できた時刻を一つの欄へ、確かでない人物や物の特徴を別の欄へ書きました。背の高さやかばんの色は手がかりにはなっても、本人や物を特定する証拠ではないと明確になりました。職員も後の落とし物報告で同じ形式を使うようになりました。

questions.prompt: What was the committee's main lesson from the lost-bag case?
questions.answer: They needed to separate confirmed observations from guesses before deciding who had moved the bag.
questions.evidence: The committee separated direct observations from guesses.
questions.evidenceJp: 委員会は直接見たことと推測を分けました。
questions.reason: The case shows that different accounts should be checked against confirmed evidence before making an accusation.

questions.prompt: Why did the 1:18 photo weaken the suspicion about the tall person?
questions.answer: Because it showed that the missing bag was still on the bench shortly before Student B's report about a tall person carrying a dark bag away.
questions.evidence: They checked a photo taken at 1:18 and saw the missing bag still on the bench.
questions.evidenceJp: 1時18分に撮られた写真を確認すると、なくなったかばんはまだベンチにありました。
questions.reason: The photo provided direct time-stamped evidence that did not support treating Student B's description as proof that the missing bag had been taken.

questions.prompt: Where was the missing bag eventually found?
questions.answer: At the information desk, where a staff member had moved it for safety.
questions.evidence: Later, the owner found it at the information desk, where a staff member had moved it for safety.
questions.evidenceJp: 後で持ち主は案内所でかばんを見つけました。安全のため職員が移していたのです。
questions.reason: This is the confirmed explanation for why the bag was no longer on the bench.

questions.prompt: Why was Student B's description useful but insufficient by itself?
questions.answer: It offered a possible lead, but Student B had not seen the bench and could not confirm that the dark bag was the missing one.
questions.evidence: Others pointed out that Student B had not seen the bench and could not identify the bag.
questions.evidenceJp: しかしBはベンチそのものを見ておらず、そのかばんが同じ物だと確認できていないという意見も出ました。
questions.reason: A description can guide checking, but it cannot establish identity when the observer did not confirm the object itself.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: The committee avoided an unsupported accusation by building a careful ____ from confirmed observations.
questions.answer: timeline
questions.evidence: The careful timeline prevented an unsupported accusation.
questions.evidenceJp: 時系列を丁寧に確認したことで、根拠のない非難を避けられました。
questions.reason: The confirmed sequence of events was the key method used to test the competing accounts.

questionSetB.prompt: What did Student A report seeing at 1:10?
questionSetB.answer: The bag on the bench.
questionSetB.evidence: Student A said she saw the bag on the bench at 1:10.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: Aは1時10分にベンチの上にかばんを見たと言いました。
questionSetB.reason: Student A's statement gives one confirmed time point in the sequence.

questionSetB.prompt: What did the committee write in separate columns?
questionSetB.answer: Confirmed times in one column and uncertain descriptions in another.
questionSetB.evidence: The committee wrote the confirmed times in one column and uncertain descriptions in another.

questionSetB.reason: The two-column format visibly separated stronger evidence from uncertain information.

questionSetB.prompt: In the passage, what does 'leads' mean in the statement that height and bag color were useful leads?
questionSetB.answer: Clues worth checking, but not proof of identity.

questionSetB.reason: The contrast with 'not proof' shows that leads are clues that guide further investigation rather than final evidence.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did staff later use the same reporting format for other lost-property cases?

passages.title: The Audio Tour with Long Pauses
passages.body: Museum volunteers tested two versions of an audio tour. Version A gave the information quickly with almost no pause. Version B used the same information but included long pauses after every sentence. Visitors using Version A often finished, but some said they needed more time to look at objects. Visitors using Version B had enough looking time but sometimes felt the tour was slow and stopped it. The team created Version C with short pauses only after important descriptions and before visitors moved to the next object. In a new test, more visitors completed the tour and reported that the pace felt comfortable. The team did not remove historical information; it changed when listeners were given time to look. The volunteers also checked whether age affected the result. Younger and older visitors preferred slightly different speeds, but both groups completed Version C more often than Version B. The museum therefore kept one main version and added a pause button reminder at the start for anyone who wanted extra viewing time.
passages.fullTranslation: 博物館のボランティアは音声案内の二つの版を試しました。A版はほとんど間を置かず、情報を速く伝えました。B版は同じ情報を使いながら、すべての文の後に長い間を入れました。A版を使った来館者は最後まで聞く人が多い一方、展示を見る時間がもっと欲しいという声がありました。B版では見る時間は十分でしたが、遅く感じて途中でやめる人がいました。チームは、重要な説明の後と次の展示へ移る前だけ短い間を入れたC版を作りました。新しいテストでは最後まで聞く人が増え、進み方がちょうどよいという感想も増えました。歴史情報を削ったのではなく、見る時間を与える位置を変えたのです。 ボランティアは年齢による違いも確認しました。若い来館者と年齢の高い来館者では好む速さに少し差がありましたが、どちらもB版よりC版を最後まで聞く割合が高くなりました。そこで博物館は基本版を一つにし、もっと見る時間が欲しい人のため開始時に一時停止ボタンの案内を加えました。

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: Version C improved the tour by placing short pauses at ____ moments instead of after every sentence.

questionSetB.prompt: What result did the new test of Version C show?

passages.title: The Temporary Shelter Room Plan
passages.body: After a large storm warning, a community center prepared three rooms as a temporary shelter. Room A held forty people and was closest to the entrance. Room B held twenty and had a sink. Room C held thirty and was the quietest room. Four family groups were expected: twelve older adults, eight families with small children totaling twenty-four people, ten adults who needed no special support, and six people who used mobility aids. Supplies would arrive in two deliveries. Water and blankets would arrive at 5:00 p.m., while baby supplies and extra floor mats would arrive at 6:30. The planning students placed the six people using mobility aids and twelve older adults in Room A because it had the easiest entrance route. The twenty-four people in families with small children could not fit in Room B, even though its sink was useful. They used Room C for most of those families and placed four people from that group in Room B with the ten other adults. The students reserved space near Room B's sink for baby-care use after the 6:30 delivery. Their plan also kept each room below capacity and left a clear path to the entrance. The room choices balanced access, quiet, useful facilities, family size, and delivery timing rather than giving every special group the room with the most obvious feature. The students then tested the room plan against two changes. First, they assumed four additional adults might arrive after 6:00. Rooms A and B still had enough unused capacity for them without moving the families. Second, they considered what would happen if the 6:30 delivery was delayed. Baby-care space near the sink would still be available, but volunteers would need to keep a small emergency set from existing supplies. The entrance map marked a wide route to Room A and prohibited boxes from being stored along it. Room C received a quiet-area sign because young children might sleep there, while louder information announcements were made near Rooms A and B. Each room leader received a list showing current room totals, free spaces, and the location of water after the first delivery. The final plan was not permanent; students wrote that assignments should change if a person's health or mobility needs changed. By checking both capacity and possible disruptions, they made the shelter plan flexible rather than merely fitting everyone into the rooms once.
passages.fullTranslation: 大きな嵐の警報を受け、地域センターは三つの部屋を一時避難所として準備しました。A室は40人で入口に最も近く、B室は20人で流しがあり、C室は30人で最も静かな部屋です。避難予定は、高齢者12人、小さな子どものいる家族計24人、特別な支援を必要としない大人10人、移動補助具を使う6人でした。物資は二回に分けて届きます。水と毛布は午後5時、乳幼児用品と追加の床用マットは6時30分です。計画を担当した生徒たちは、入口までの道が最も使いやすいA室に、移動補助具を使う6人と高齢者12人を配置しました。小さな子どものいる24人は、流しが便利でも定員20人のB室には全員入りません。そのため多くをC室へ入れ、そのグループの4人を、ほかの大人10人とともにB室へ配置しました。6時30分の物資到着後に乳幼児の世話ができるよう、B室の流し近くには場所を確保しました。どの部屋も定員を超えず、入口への通路も空けました。分かりやすい設備だけで部屋を決めず、移動しやすさ、静けさ、設備、家族人数、物資到着時刻を合わせて考えた計画です。 生徒たちはさらに二つの変化を想定して部屋割りを確かめました。まず午後6時以降に大人が4人追加で来る場合を考えました。A室とB室にはまだ空きがあり、家族を移動させなくても受け入れられます。次に6時30分の配送が遅れる場合も検討しました。流し近くの乳幼児用スペースは使えますが、それまでのために既存物資から少量の緊急用品を確保する必要があります。入口地図にはA室までの広い通路を示し、その通路には箱を置かないようにしました。C室には小さな子どもが眠る可能性を考えて静かな区域の表示を出し、大きな情報放送はA室とB室の近くで行います。各部屋の担当者には現在人数、空き人数、最初の配送後の水の場所を示す一覧を渡しました。この部屋割りは固定ではなく、体調や移動上の必要が変われば変更すると記しました。定員だけでなく起こり得る変更も確認したことで、一度全員を入れるだけではない柔軟な避難計画になりました。

questions.prompt: What was the main goal of the students' shelter plan?
questions.answer: To place people safely while balancing room capacity, access, quiet, useful facilities, family size, and delivery timing.
questions.evidence: The room choices balanced access, quiet, useful facilities, family size, and delivery timing rather than giving every special group the room with the most obvious feature.
questions.evidenceJp: 分かりやすい設備だけで部屋を決めず、移動しやすさ、静けさ、設備、家族人数、物資到着時刻を合わせて考えた計画です。
questions.reason: The plan was designed around several constraints at once, not a single feature of each room.

questions.prompt: Why were the six people using mobility aids and the twelve older adults placed in Room A?
questions.answer: Because Room A had the easiest route from the entrance.
questions.evidence: The planning students placed the six people using mobility aids and twelve older adults in Room A because it had the easiest entrance route.
questions.evidenceJp: 計画を担当した生徒たちは、入口までの道が最も使いやすいA室に、移動補助具を使う6人と高齢者12人を配置しました。
questions.reason: Easy access was especially important for people whose movement could be difficult.

questions.prompt: Why could all twenty-four people in families with small children not use Room B?
questions.answer: Because Room B held only twenty people.
questions.evidence: The twenty-four people in families with small children could not fit in Room B, even though its sink was useful.
questions.evidenceJp: 小さな子どものいる24人は、流しが便利でも定員20人のB室には全員入りません。
questions.reason: The sink was useful, but the room's capacity was smaller than the family group's total size.

questions.prompt: What does the test with four additional adults show about the plan?
questions.answer: It had enough unused capacity to handle a small increase in arrivals without moving the families.
questions.evidence: Rooms A and B still had enough unused capacity for them without moving the families.
questions.evidenceJp: A室とB室にはまだ空きがあり、家族を移動させなくても受け入れられます。
questions.reason: A flexible shelter plan should still work when the number of people changes slightly.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: The students made the shelter plan flexible by checking both room capacity and possible ____.
questions.answer: disruptions
questions.evidence: By checking both capacity and possible disruptions, they made the shelter plan flexible rather than merely fitting everyone into the rooms once.
questions.evidenceJp: 定員だけでなく起こり得る変更も確認したことで、一度全員を入れるだけではない柔軟な避難計画になりました。
questions.reason: The final sentence directly states that possible disruptions were checked in addition to capacity.

questionSetB.prompt: What two kinds of supplies were scheduled to arrive at 6:30 p.m.?
questionSetB.answer: Baby supplies and extra floor mats.
questionSetB.evidence: Water and blankets would arrive at 5:00 p.m., while baby supplies and extra floor mats would arrive at 6:30.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 水と毛布は午後5時、乳幼児用品と追加の床用マットは6時30分です。
questionSetB.reason: The second delivery contained the baby supplies and extra mats.

questionSetB.prompt: Which room feature was intentionally kept available for baby care after the second delivery?
questionSetB.answer: The space near Room B's sink.
questionSetB.evidence: The students reserved space near Room B's sink for baby-care use after the 6:30 delivery.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 6時30分の物資到着後に乳幼児の世話ができるよう、B室の流し近くには場所を確保しました。
questionSetB.reason: The room's sink was useful for baby care, so nearby space was reserved rather than filling it completely.

questionSetB.prompt: What would volunteers need to do if the 6:30 delivery was delayed?
questionSetB.answer: Keep a small emergency set from supplies already available.
questionSetB.evidence: Baby-care space near the sink would still be available, but volunteers would need to keep a small emergency set from existing supplies.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 流し近くの乳幼児用スペースは使えますが、それまでのために既存物資から少量の緊急用品を確保する必要があります。
questionSetB.reason: A delay would affect supplies, not the physical baby-care space itself.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the entrance map prohibit boxes along the wide route to Room A?
questionSetB.answer: To keep the access route clear for people using Room A.
questionSetB.evidence: The entrance map marked a wide route to Room A and prohibited boxes from being stored along it.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 入口地図にはA室までの広い通路を示し、その通路には箱を置かないようにしました。
questionSetB.reason: Keeping the route free of boxes protected the easy-access purpose of Room A.

questionSetB.prompt: Which statement best describes the final shelter assignments?
questionSetB.answer: They were a starting plan that could be changed if people's health or mobility needs changed.
questionSetB.evidence: The final plan was not permanent; students wrote that assignments should change if a person's health or mobility needs changed.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: この部屋割りは固定ではなく、体調や移動上の必要が変われば変更すると記しました。
questionSetB.reason: The students treated the assignments as adaptable rather than fixed once and for all.

passages.title: The Graph behind the Strong Claim
passages.body: The newspaper club prepared a headline saying, “New Study Space Improves Learning for Everyone.” The headline was based on a graph showing that students who used the room reported higher concentration than before. Before publishing, one member checked the survey details. Only forty students had answered, and all of them were regular users of the new room. The survey did not include students who studied elsewhere, and it measured reported concentration rather than test scores. The club changed the headline to “Regular Users Report Better Concentration in New Study Space.” The graph stayed in the article, but the text explained who had answered and what had been measured. The revised headline was less dramatic, yet it matched the evidence instead of claiming a result for every student. The article also linked the graph title directly to the survey question and stated the number of respondents. Readers could then see the difference between a report about regular users and a claim about the whole school.
passages.fullTranslation: 新聞部は「新しい学習スペースが全員の学習を改善」という見出しを準備しました。これは、その部屋を使った生徒が以前より集中できたと答えたグラフを根拠にしていました。公開前に一人の部員が調査の詳細を確認しました。回答したのは40人だけで、全員が新しい部屋を普段から使う生徒でした。別の場所で勉強する生徒は含まれておらず、測ったのもテスト点ではなく本人が感じた集中度でした。そこで見出しを「新しい学習スペースの常用者、集中しやすくなったと回答」へ変えました。グラフは記事に残しましたが、誰が答え、何を測ったかも説明しました。新しい見出しは派手さは減りましたが、すべての生徒について言い切るのではなく、証拠と一致する内容になりました。 記事ではグラフの題名もアンケート質問に直接対応させ、回答者数も示しました。これにより、常用者についての報告と学校全体についての主張の違いを読者が確認できるようになりました。

questions.prompt: Why did the newspaper club change its original headline?
questions.answer: Because the original headline claimed an effect for everyone that the survey evidence did not support.
questions.evidence: The revised headline was less dramatic, yet it matched the evidence instead of claiming a result for every student.
questions.evidenceJp: 新しい見出しは派手さは減りましたが、すべての生徒について言い切るのではなく、証拠と一致する内容になりました。
questions.reason: The club changed the claim so that it matched the actual limits of the survey.

questions.prompt: Who answered the survey?
questions.answer: Forty students who were regular users of the new study room.
questions.evidence: Only forty students had answered, and all of them were regular users of the new room.
questions.evidenceJp: 回答したのは40人だけで、全員が新しい部屋を普段から使う生徒でした。
questions.reason: The sample was limited to regular users rather than the whole school.

questions.prompt: Why was it inaccurate to say the study space improved learning for everyone?
questions.answer: Because the survey excluded students who studied elsewhere and measured reported concentration rather than test scores.
questions.evidence: The survey did not include students who studied elsewhere, and it measured reported concentration rather than test scores.
questions.evidenceJp: 別の場所で勉強する生徒は含まれておらず、測ったのもテスト点ではなく本人が感じた集中度でした。
questions.reason: The participants and the thing measured were both narrower than the original headline suggested.

questions.prompt: What part of the article stayed after the headline was revised?
questions.answer: The graph stayed in the article.
questions.evidence: The graph stayed in the article, but the text explained who had answered and what had been measured.
questions.evidenceJp: グラフは記事に残しましたが、誰が答え、何を測ったかも説明しました。
questions.reason: The club kept the evidence but added context so readers could interpret it correctly.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: The club made the article more accurate by matching the headline to the survey's ____.
questions.answer: evidence
questions.evidence: The revised headline was less dramatic, yet it matched the evidence instead of claiming a result for every student.
questions.evidenceJp: 新しい見出しは派手さは減りましたが、すべての生徒について言い切るのではなく、証拠と一致する内容になりました。
questions.reason: The central revision was to make the claim no broader than the evidence allowed.

questionSetB.prompt: What problem could occur if readers saw only the original headline and graph?
questionSetB.answer: They might wrongly think the survey proved that the new room improved learning for every student.
questionSetB.evidence: The revised headline was less dramatic, yet it matched the evidence instead of claiming a result for every student.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 新しい見出しは派手さは減りましたが、すべての生徒について言い切るのではなく、証拠と一致する内容になりました。
questionSetB.reason: Without the survey limits, readers could generalize a result from regular users to the whole school.

questionSetB.prompt: In this passage, what does 'respondents' mean?
questionSetB.answer: The people who answered the survey.
questionSetB.evidence: The article also linked the graph title directly to the survey question and stated the number of respondents.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 記事ではグラフの題名もアンケート質問に直接対応させ、回答者数も示しました。
questionSetB.reason: The surrounding sentences discuss the forty students who answered the survey.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the article state the number of respondents?
questionSetB.answer: So readers could see how limited the survey sample was.
questionSetB.evidence: The article also linked the graph title directly to the survey question and stated the number of respondents.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 記事ではグラフの題名もアンケート質問に直接対応させ、回答者数も示しました。
questionSetB.reason: Giving the sample size helps readers judge how far the result can reasonably be generalized.

questionSetB.prompt: What did the survey actually measure?
questionSetB.answer: Students' reported concentration.
questionSetB.evidence: The survey did not include students who studied elsewhere, and it measured reported concentration rather than test scores.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 別の場所で勉強する生徒は含まれておらず、測ったのもテスト点ではなく本人が感じた集中度でした。
questionSetB.reason: The passage clearly distinguishes reported concentration from objective test-score improvement.

questionSetB.prompt: What lesson about reporting data does the passage show?
questionSetB.answer: A claim should identify who was studied and what was actually measured instead of making a broader statement than the data support.
questionSetB.evidence: Readers could then see the difference between a report about regular users and a claim about the whole school.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: これにより、常用者についての報告と学校全体についての主張の違いを読者が確認できるようになりました。
questionSetB.reason: The article became more trustworthy when it separated the actual sample result from a claim about everyone.

passages.title: The Stream Record from Two Seasons
passages.body: Students compared water-quality records from a local stream in spring and autumn. The autumn sheet showed clearer water and a lower reading for one pollution indicator. Some students wanted to report that the stream had improved. Before writing the conclusion, the group checked the measurement conditions. The spring sample had been taken the morning after heavy rain, while the autumn sample came after five dry days. The sampling times were also different. Rain could carry soil and other material into the stream, so the two measurements were not directly comparable. The students collected another sample after similar dry weather and at the same time of day as the autumn test. The new result was closer to the autumn record. Their report said the first comparison was inconclusive and explained what conditions needed to match before judging long-term change. The group scheduled future sampling for the first Friday of each month at the same hour and planned to record recent rainfall beside every result. They noted that matching conditions would not remove every difference, but it would make changes easier to interpret.
passages.fullTranslation: 生徒たちは地域の小川について、春と秋の水質記録を比べました。秋の記録は水がより澄み、ある汚れの指標も低くなっていました。小川が改善したと報告したいという生徒もいました。しかし結論を書く前に測定条件を確認しました。春の採水は大雨の翌朝で、秋は雨が降らない日が五日続いた後でした。採水時刻も違っていました。雨は土やほかの物を小川へ運ぶ可能性があるため、二つをそのまま比べることはできません。生徒たちは秋の調査と同じような乾いた天候の後、同じ時刻にもう一度採水しました。新しい結果は秋の記録に近くなりました。最初の比較だけでは結論を出せないと報告し、長期的な変化を判断するにはどの条件をそろえる必要があるか説明しました。 グループは今後、毎月最初の金曜日の同じ時刻に採水し、各結果の横に直前の降雨量も記録することにしました。条件をそろえてもすべての違いがなくなるわけではありませんが、変化の意味を判断しやすくなると考えました。

slashRows.jp: ある汚れの指標も低くなっていました。

slashRows.en: Some students wanted to report
slashRows.jp: 小川が改善したと

slashRows.en: that the stream had improved.
slashRows.jp: 報告したいという生徒もいました。

slashRows.en: Before writing the conclusion,
slashRows.jp: しかし結論を書く前に、

slashRows.en: the group checked the measurement conditions.
slashRows.jp: グループは測定条件を確認しました。

slashRows.en: The spring sample had been taken the morning after heavy rain,
slashRows.jp: 春の採水は大雨の翌朝で、

slashRows.en: while the autumn sample came after five dry days.
slashRows.jp: 秋は雨が降らない日が五日続いた後でした。

slashRows.en: The sampling times were also different.
slashRows.jp: 採水時刻も違っていました。

slashRows.en: Rain could carry soil and other material into the stream,
slashRows.jp: 雨は土やほかの物を小川へ運ぶ可能性があるため、

slashRows.en: so the two measurements were not directly comparable.
slashRows.jp: 二つをそのまま比べることはできません。

slashRows.en: The students collected another sample
slashRows.jp: 生徒たちはもう一度採水し、

slashRows.en: after similar dry weather
slashRows.jp: 秋の調査と同じような乾いた天候の後、

slashRows.en: and at the same time of day as the autumn test.
slashRows.jp: 同じ時刻に調べました。

slashRows.en: The new result was closer to the autumn record.
slashRows.jp: 新しい結果は秋の記録に近くなりました。

slashRows.en: Their report said
slashRows.jp: 報告では、

slashRows.en: the first comparison was inconclusive
slashRows.jp: 最初の比較だけでは結論を出せないとし、

slashRows.en: and explained what conditions needed to match
slashRows.jp: どの条件をそろえる必要があるか説明しました。

slashRows.en: before judging long-term change.
slashRows.jp: 長期的な変化を判断するためです。

slashRows.en: The group scheduled future sampling
slashRows.jp: グループは今後の採水を決め、

slashRows.en: for the first Friday of each month at the same hour
slashRows.jp: 毎月最初の金曜日の同じ時刻に行い、

slashRows.en: and planned to record recent rainfall beside every result.
slashRows.jp: 各結果の横に直前の降雨量も記録することにしました。

slashRows.en: They noted
slashRows.jp: また、

slashRows.en: that matching conditions would not remove every difference,
slashRows.jp: 条件をそろえてもすべての違いがなくなるわけではないが、

slashRows.en: but it would make changes easier to interpret.
slashRows.jp: 変化の意味を判断しやすくなると考えました。

questions.prompt: Why did the students decide that the spring and autumn records could not be compared directly?
questions.answer: Because the samples were taken under different weather and time conditions.
questions.evidence: The spring sample had been taken the morning after heavy rain, while the autumn sample came after five dry days.
questions.evidenceJp: 春の採水は大雨の翌朝で、秋は雨が降らない日が五日続いた後でした。
questions.reason: Different recent rainfall conditions could change the stream before the samples were taken.

questions.prompt: What additional difference did the students notice besides the recent weather?
questions.answer: The sampling times were different.
questions.evidence: The sampling times were also different.
questions.evidenceJp: 採水時刻も違っていました。
questions.reason: Time of sampling was another condition that needed to be considered.

questions.prompt: Why could heavy rain affect the water-quality comparison?
questions.answer: Because rain could carry soil and other material into the stream.
questions.evidence: Rain could carry soil and other material into the stream, so the two measurements were not directly comparable.
questions.evidenceJp: 雨は土やほかの物を小川へ運ぶ可能性があるため、二つをそのまま比べることはできません。
questions.reason: Rain could change the stream temporarily, making one measurement different for reasons unrelated to long-term improvement.

questions.prompt: What did the students do before making a stronger conclusion?
questions.answer: They collected another sample after similar dry weather and at the same time of day as the autumn test.
questions.evidence: The students collected another sample after similar dry weather and at the same time of day as the autumn test.
questions.evidenceJp: 生徒たちは秋の調査と同じような乾いた天候の後、同じ時刻にもう一度採水しました。
questions.reason: They tried to make the sampling conditions more comparable before interpreting the result.

questions.prompt: Complete the summary: The first spring-autumn comparison was judged ____ because the measurement conditions did not match.
questions.answer: inconclusive
questions.evidence: Their report said the first comparison was inconclusive and explained what conditions needed to match before judging long-term change.
questions.evidenceJp: 最初の比較だけでは結論を出せないと報告し、長期的な変化を判断するにはどの条件をそろえる必要があるか説明しました。
questions.reason: The students could not tell whether the difference represented a real long-term change from the first two samples alone.

questionSetB.prompt: What did the new sample suggest about the autumn result?
questionSetB.answer: It suggested that similar dry-weather conditions could produce a result close to the autumn record.
questionSetB.evidence: The new result was closer to the autumn record.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 新しい結果は秋の記録に近くなりました。
questionSetB.reason: The closer result after matching weather and time conditions showed that conditions mattered to the comparison.

questionSetB.prompt: How did the students plan to make future sampling more consistent?
questionSetB.answer: They planned to sample on the first Friday of each month at the same hour and record recent rainfall.
questionSetB.evidence: The group scheduled future sampling for the first Friday of each month at the same hour and planned to record recent rainfall beside every result.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: グループは今後、毎月最初の金曜日の同じ時刻に採水し、各結果の横に直前の降雨量も記録することにしました。
questionSetB.reason: A regular schedule plus rainfall records would make later comparisons easier to interpret.

questionSetB.prompt: In this passage, what does 'inconclusive' mean?
questionSetB.answer: Not strong enough to support a clear conclusion.
questionSetB.evidence: Their report said the first comparison was inconclusive and explained what conditions needed to match before judging long-term change.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 最初の比較だけでは結論を出せないと報告し、長期的な変化を判断するにはどの条件をそろえる必要があるか説明しました。
questionSetB.reason: The word describes a comparison that cannot yet justify a firm judgment.

questionSetB.prompt: Why did the group plan to record recent rainfall beside every result?
questionSetB.answer: Because rainfall could affect stream conditions and needed to be considered when comparing results over time.
questionSetB.evidence: Rain could carry soil and other material into the stream, so the two measurements were not directly comparable.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 雨は土やほかの物を小川へ運ぶ可能性があるため、二つをそのまま比べることはできません。
questionSetB.reason: Recording rainfall gives context that helps explain whether a change may be caused by weather rather than a long-term trend.

questionSetB.prompt: What principle guided the students' final monitoring plan?
questionSetB.answer: Make important measurement conditions as consistent as possible and record remaining factors that could affect interpretation.
questionSetB.evidence: They noted that matching conditions would not remove every difference, but it would make changes easier to interpret.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 条件をそろえてもすべての違いがなくなるわけではありませんが、変化の意味を判断しやすくなると考えました。
questionSetB.reason: The students did not expect perfect control, but they improved the reliability of future comparisons.
